Audit method:
1. Build a full file/line manifest for the target scope.
2. Run static scans for fallback/compatibility/legacy/default/inference markers.
3. Extract exported functions and repeated helper names to locate independently implemented API surfaces.
4. Read high-signal modules line-by-line and record confirmed findings with file/line references.
5. Keep this ledger updated after each batch so progress survives context loss.

Open findings:
- F01 Workspace storage keeps a legacy toolbar compatibility layer.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/shell/workspace-storage.mjs:25-52` migrates flat `commandIds`, `hiddenCommandIds`, `groupIds`, `collapsedGroups`, `dock`, and `modeling` into `toolbars.modeling`; `:56-63` still imports the legacy shape; `:135-156` owns legacy shape detection and field extraction.
  Risk: Every read/write/import passes through migration, so old UI storage shape remains a live branch in normal runtime code.
  Recommendation: If migration from the old localStorage/export format is no longer required, remove `hasLegacyModelingToolbar`/`legacyModelingToolbar`; otherwise move it to a named one-time importer and keep runtime storage current-shape-only.

- F02 Dev server accepts both canonical and legacy encoded branch URL prefixes.
  Evidence: `scripts/serve_viewer.js:98-108` builds both `/{branch parts}` and `/{encodeURIComponent(branch)}` prefixes; `:179-183` strips either form.
  Risk: The preview URL contract says `/codex/agentN/...` is required, but the server still supports `/codex%2FagentN/...`.
  Recommendation: Remove `legacyEncodedBranchPathPrefix` once old links are not needed, or document the deprecation window.

- F03 Object trim region keys still carry legacy aliases.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/trim-region-geometry.mjs:116-125` strips `:owner_...:cutter_...` from feature ids and returns both canonical and legacy `objectTrimRegionKey` aliases.
  Risk: Region removal accepts two identities for the same derived part, which makes future data migrations and UI display of region keys harder to reason about.
  Recommendation: Migrate existing sample/project data to canonical region keys, then remove the alias path; until then, document it as an explicit compatibility layer.

- F04 Planned commands are visible product surface with no real implementation path.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/command-registry.mjs:197-228` registers Clash Detection and Structural Analysis as `status: "planned", implemented: false`; `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-command-registration.mjs:346-348` has an empty `plannedModelCommandState`; `:648-653` handlers only set "not available yet" status text.
  Risk: The command registry, navbar, palette, state resolver, and handler map all carry placeholder workflow branches.
  Recommendation: Either hide unimplemented commands from runtime surfaces or centralize planned-command state/handler behavior from command metadata instead of registering bespoke no-op handlers.

- F05 Validation helpers are copied across engine API modules instead of inherited from one validator contract.
  Evidence: repeated local `fail`, `requiredObject`, `optionalObject`, `optionalString`, `requiredString`, `requiredVec3`, and number validators appear in `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/semantic-builders.mjs:48-113`, `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/axis-relations.mjs:10-29`, `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/member-factory.mjs:8-84`, `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/transport-sectioning.mjs:9-60`, `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/shared/validation.mjs:1-58`, and `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-runtime-validation.mjs:15-75`.
  Context: `bobercad/app/engine/core/math.mjs:20-49` and `bobercad/app/engine/core/model.mjs:3-20` already provide some primitives, but not a complete error-context validator API.
  Recommendation: Add one shared validation module with domain error prefixes/context adapters, then migrate module-local required/optional helpers onto it.

- F06 2D/3D geometry primitives are partly duplicated.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/geometry.mjs:17-48` defines local vector/plate point validation, and `:103-114` defines a local 2D `pointInPolygon`; `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/polygon.mjs:68-79` has another private point-in-polygon implementation for projected polygon points.
  Risk: Boundary behavior and tolerance rules can drift between model API geometry and rendering/CSG geometry.
  Recommendation: Promote a shared 2D polygon predicate and vec/point validator API, then call it from model geometry, snap, and polygon modules.

- F07 Inspector metadata duplicates formatting and object-reference action helpers.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-editable-object-property-metadata.mjs:482-523`, `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-property-metadata.mjs:857-865` plus `:1124-1141`, and `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-support-object-property-metadata.mjs:125-147` plus `:590-607` repeat object ref action specs, numeric/vector formatting, `finiteNumber`, `finiteNumberOr`, `objectMap`, and `arrayValues`.
  Risk: Inspector panels can diverge in numeric formatting, object-reference actions, and missing-value behavior, so the same object field can feel or behave differently depending on which inspector metadata file renders it.
  Recommendation: Extract shared `inspector-formatting` and `object-ref-actions` helpers under `bobercad/app/ui/commands/`, then make editable/support/main metadata use the same surface.

- F08 Snap strength is defined in two places.
  Evidence: UI metadata has `SNAP_STRENGTH_SPECS` and `normalizeSnapStrength` in `bobercad/app/ui/commands/snap-metadata.mjs:1-58`; runtime profile code separately has `SNAP_STRENGTHS` and `normalizedStrength` in `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-profiles.mjs:3` and `:92-95`.
  Risk: Adding or renaming a snap strength requires synchronized edits in UI metadata and runtime profile resolution.
  Recommendation: Put strength ids/specs in one runtime-safe shared module and let UI add labels/descriptions around the shared ids.

- F09 Shortcut setting fallback logic is duplicated.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/keyboard-shortcuts.mjs:77-79` exports `shortcutSetting`, while `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/panel-elements.mjs:596-598` defines the same `hasOwnProperty` fallback helper locally.
  Risk: Keyboard shortcut default behavior can drift between runtime shortcut handling and panel rendering, especially when a setting is intentionally `false` or missing.
  Recommendation: Import the existing keyboard shortcut helper in `panel-elements.mjs`.

- F10 Project model/object access helpers are duplicated across API, store, and Smart Component runtime layers.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/objects.mjs:47-59` has private `projectModel`, `projectObjectIndex`, `modelCollection`; `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:58-68` exports equivalent store helpers and many typed `*ById` helpers; `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-model-helpers.mjs:15-27` defines another `projectModel/projectObjectIndex/projectCollection` surface plus its own `MODEL_COLLECTIONS`.
  Risk: Collection names, missing-object behavior, whether a missing collection is created, and error prefixes can drift between normal project API commands, store mutation helpers, and Smart Component generation.
  Recommendation: Promote one public project object-access module that owns collection registration, objectIndex validation, collection lookup, and typed `byId` behavior; let store and Smart Component helpers wrap that only for mutation-specific behavior.

- F11 Datum/grid geometry has hidden fallback axes despite the schema requiring explicit grid axes.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:598-609` requires grid systems to store `origin`, `axisX`, `axisY`, `axisZ`, and `axes`; `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/datums.mjs:58-76` still falls back to `[0,0,0]`, inferred `axisX/axisY/axisZ`, and a `rotation` field when axes are missing or invalid. `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-datum-reference-assembly.mjs:40-52` renders grid systems through `allGridLineSegments`, so this fallback can affect viewer geometry.
  Risk: Invalid or old grid data can still render/snap with invented axes instead of failing validation, which conflicts with the explicit-datum source-of-truth rule.
  Recommendation: Split strict datum evaluation from any legacy importer. Runtime rendering/snapping should require schema-valid axes; a migration/import path can convert old `rotation`-style grid data once.

- F12 Fastener/hole diameter derivation is implemented in one primitive but bypassed in other connection primitives.
  Evidence: Data-model rule `docs/architecture/data-model.md:206` says hole diameter should be derived from `fastenerRef` plus `holes.tolerance`/`holes.customDiameter`. `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/fasteners/secondary-web-bolting.mjs:12-27` implements catalog-based `holeDiameter` and `holeType`; `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/smart-component-parameter-values.mjs:10-25` has another UI-side `fastenerHoleDiameter` derivation. But `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/plates/member-end-plate.mjs:84-96`, `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/plates/base-plate.mjs:27-45`, and `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/plates/dual-member-gusset.mjs:97-113` still require direct `holes.diameter`.
  Risk: Different connection generators can disagree on hole diameter and tolerance behavior; adding a catalog tolerance requires checking multiple independent implementations.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared fastener/hole derivation primitive used by all through-bolting generators, then let configs expose tolerance/custom diameter instead of raw diameter where appropriate.

- F13 Left-dock data panels share DOM primitives but still duplicate panel lifecycle/search/focus scaffolding.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/project-data-panel.mjs:57-113`, `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/project-files-panel.mjs:63-121`, `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/project-properties-panel.mjs:63-92`, `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/model-browser.mjs:84-127`, and `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/smart-component-browser.mjs:90-137` repeat query state, renderSearch, focusSearch restoration, and row/preset focusing patterns around the same `dataPanelSearch`/`dataPanelHeader` primitives from `bobercad/app/ui/design-system/ui-elements.mjs:826-905`.
  Risk: Search focus behavior, dataset naming, and empty-state behavior can diverge between panels even though the user-facing interaction is the same.
  Recommendation: Introduce a small data-panel controller/helper for query state, search rendering, focus restoration, and row lookup. Keep each panel responsible only for its domain rows/sections.

- F14 Snap solver contains an active compatibility layer for candidate shape.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/interaction/snap-solver.mjs:106-142` creates canonical `geometry`, `identity`, `visibility`, `ranking`, `reference`, `hints`, and `preview` fields but falls back to flat candidate fields such as `kind`, `point`, `a`, `b`, `origin`, `normal`, `providerId`, `type`, `objectId`, `target`, `visibilityPolicy`, `screenTolerance`, `visibilityPenaltyPx`, and `relationHints`. `:145-173` validates the flat fields before applying canonical fields.
  Risk: Snap providers can keep emitting mixed old/new candidate shapes indefinitely, so candidate contract drift is hidden in the solver instead of failing at provider boundaries.
  Recommendation: Define one canonical snap-candidate DTO and either migrate all providers to emit it or move this normalizer to an explicitly named one-time/provider-adapter layer with diagnostics for legacy flat fields.

- F15 Fin-plate bolting diagnostics still reference the old/direct hole diameter parameter path.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/fasteners/secondary-web-bolting.mjs:156-161` derives `effectiveHoleDiameter` from `holes.tolerance` and `holes.customDiameter`, but the grid-fit diagnostics list `holes.diameter` in `parameterPaths` at `:240-247` and `:248-257`.
  Risk: UI diagnostics and auto-resolve hints can point users to a parameter that this generator no longer reads, while other primitives still use direct `holes.diameter`. This blurs the intended standard from F12.
  Recommendation: Replace `holes.diameter` diagnostic paths with `holes.tolerance` and `holes.customDiameter` where relevant, and finish standardizing all connection primitives on the same hole-diameter derivation contract.

- F16 Secondary-web connection primitives can use either injected cached context or recomputed context.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/shared/secondary-web-context.mjs:19-24` returns `recipeContext.connectionContext` when present; otherwise `:26-98` recomputes context from interfaces, members, profiles, plate params, fit params, and geometry. `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/plates/secondary-web-plate.mjs:101` returns `{ connectionContext: context, ... }`, making the injected path active for later primitives.
  Risk: Later primitives can depend on a context snapshot produced by an earlier primitive, while the same helper also supports recomputation. That makes operation ordering and stale context harder to reason about.
  Recommendation: Make connection context creation an explicit pipeline step or shared runtime input, then remove the implicit "use cached if present, else recompute" branch from primitive helpers.

- F17 Connection primitive generators use both raw `ctx.param` and default/diagnostic-aware `ctx.parameterValue` for required parameters.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/plates/base-plate.mjs:123-124` reads `welds.column` via `ctx.param`; `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/plates/member-end-plate.mjs:146-149` reads `welds.beamWeb` via `ctx.param`; `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/stiffeners/support-web-stiffeners.mjs:73-75` reads `welds.top` and `welds.bottom` via `ctx.param`. The same files and neighboring primitives use `ctx.parameterValue`/`ctx.params` for other required/defaulted parameters.
  Risk: Some generator parameters can bypass definition defaults and missing-parameter diagnostics while others do not, depending on which primitive authored them.
  Recommendation: Standardize generator parameter access: reserve `ctx.param` for explicitly raw reads, otherwise migrate required primitive parameters to `ctx.parameterValue`/`ctx.params` with clear required/default behavior.

- F18 Smart Component semantic builder has public methods and normalization rules outside the API register/store contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/semantic-builders.mjs:185-578` returns builder namespaces for `member`, `reference`, `trim`, `part`, `pattern`, `feature`, `fastener`, `weld`, `assembly`, `workPoint`, and `objectPattern`; `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:106-112` attaches them onto the runtime context and overloads `ctx.member` as both the existing-member accessor and a method namespace. `api-register.json:74-80` documents only read-style `ctx.member`, and `api-register.json:303-410` documents only part of the semantic builder surface; entries for `ctx.member.beam`, `ctx.member.column`, `ctx.assembly.create`, `ctx.workPoint.create`, and `ctx.objectPattern.create` were not found. Those omitted methods are used by component libraries, for example `bobercad/data/libraries/smart-components/components/frames/portal-frame/build.mjs:17-50`, `bobercad/data/libraries/smart-components/components/stairs/landings/shared-landing.mjs:99-120`, and `bobercad/data/libraries/smart-components/components/stairs/railings/shared/railing-path-and-panel-system.mjs:147-736`. The same file also creates trim joints directly in `semantic-builders.mjs:177-316`, while store-side trim creation/updates use `normalizedTrimJointOperation` and `validateTrimJointOperation` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:569-704` through `project-store-trim-methods.mjs:21-63` and `:117-135`.
  Risk: The actual public Smart Component API is wider than the register says, and generated trim objects can evolve under semantic-builder rules that are parallel to, rather than inherited from, the store trim-normalization rules.
  Recommendation: Make `api-register.json` enumerate the real semantic builder surface, split read access from creation namespaces where possible, and route trim builder operations through the same normalization/validation helper used by project-store trim APIs.

- F19 Smart Component parameter values are resolved differently in UI and runtime, so derived values are reimplemented instead of inherited.
  Evidence: UI-facing `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/smart-component-parameter-values.mjs:54-65` resolves derived kinds such as `fastenerHoleDiameter`, `spacingList`, `boltEdgeDistance`, and `sameAsParameter`; runtime `ctx.parameterValue` in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:148-159` only reads stored values or definition defaults. The fin-plate config defines derived `holes.diameter` in `bobercad/data/libraries/smart-components/components/connections/fin-plate/config.json:365-381`, while the fin-plate bolting primitive independently derives `effectiveHoleDiameter` from catalog/tolerance/custom diameter in `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/connection-primitives/fasteners/secondary-web-bolting.mjs:156-161`. Definition validation in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-parameters-and-definition.mjs:172-182` validates parameter kind basics but does not validate the live `derive`, `writePath`, `editableWhen`, or `standardOptions` schemas used by `smart-component-parameter-values.mjs:56-59`, `:118-123`, `:166-179`, `:249-252`, and `:337-344`.
  Risk: The UI can display/edit a derived parameter value that runtime builders cannot read through the same `ctx.parameterValue` contract, forcing each generator to reimplement derivations. Invalid derived-parameter config can also survive definition validation and degrade silently at UI resolution time.
  Recommendation: Promote one Smart Component parameter resolver/derive schema used by UI, runtime build context, validation, and generator APIs. Derived display-only parameters should be explicitly marked as UI-only; generator-consumed derived values should resolve through the same runtime API.

- F20 Smart Component diagnostics still emit and display a legacy `parameters` alias while new APIs reject `parameters`.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/solver-result.mjs:57` rejects diagnostic input field `parameters` and requires `parameterPaths`; `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/checks.mjs:58-62` and `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/compliance.mjs:86-98` enforce the same canonical name. But `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:121-137` rejects incoming `details.parameters` and then emits both `parameterPaths` and `parameters` when `parameterPaths` is provided. The UI still reads the alias in `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/smart-component-parameter-ui.mjs:77-86`.
  Risk: Callers see a mixed contract: authoring APIs tell them `parameters` is unsupported, but generated diagnostics still contain and display it. That keeps the old field live and makes future diagnostic schema cleanup risky.
  Recommendation: Migrate UI display to `parameterPaths`, add a temporary read adapter only if old project files need it, and stop emitting `parameters` from new runtime diagnostics.

- F21 Transport sectioning exposes undocumented `ctx.*` methods and downgrades named strategies to count-based object batching.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/transport-sectioning.mjs:151-233` implements estimates, sections, max-weight splitting, and schedules; `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:221-240` exposes `ctx.transportSections` and `ctx.transportSectionSchedule`, but `api-register.json:459-468` only documents generic `model.sectioning`, with no `ctx.transportSections`/`ctx.transportSectionSchedule` entries. The stair transport component calls these runtime methods in `bobercad/data/libraries/smart-components/components/stairs/sections/transport-sections/build.mjs:108-113`. For `manual-stations`, it passes `sectionCount: manualStations.length + 1` and stores `manualStations` only as metadata; for `landings`, it passes a count based on source component count. Runtime `transportSections` then chunks the object estimate array by index in `smart-component-build.mjs:230-236`.
  Risk: A user-facing strategy name such as `manual-stations` implies geometric/station-based splitting, but the runtime currently partitions object ids by count. That can produce believable transport section records while ignoring the actual station values and split frames.
  Recommendation: Register the `ctx.transport*` APIs explicitly, then either implement strategy-specific sectioning using split frames/stations or rename the current behavior as count-based grouping and keep station metadata out of the strategy contract.

- F22 Axis relation project API directly parses rendering snap DTOs and carries grid-line defaults/aliases.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/axis-relations.mjs:82-130` converts snap candidates by inspecting `snap.kind`, `snap.type`, flat `snap.axis`, `snap.objectId`, `snap.a`, `snap.b`, `snap.point`, and `snap.reference`; rendering interaction code calls it with live snap objects in `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/member-transform-edit-controller.mjs:650-689`, and smart-component helper code persists auto snap relations in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-helpers.mjs:108-113`. The relation id helpers accept `source.gridSystemId || source.gridId` at `axis-relations.mjs:55-63`, while grid-line resolution uses only `gridSystemId`; `axisForSource` defaults a missing grid `levelId` to the first level at `:217-226` and treats missing `axisId` as a wildcard at `:222-226`.
  Risk: A project/model API now depends on the current rendering snap candidate shape, including legacy/alternate source id naming and implicit grid defaults. Snap DTO migrations or multi-level grids can change persisted relation behavior without a clear model-level adapter boundary.
  Recommendation: Move snap-to-axis-source conversion into the interaction layer or a named adapter, then make project relations accept a canonical `source` object with explicit grid system, level, axis group, and axis id requirements.

- F23 Snap selection bypasses the central Smart Component ownership/dependency API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/dependencies.mjs:170-198` centralizes Smart Component owned/detached/connection-zone object traversal, including nested child components. `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-object-visibility.mjs:1-8` correctly imports that central helper. But `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-selection-manager.mjs:55-89` defines its own `smartComponentObjectIds(project, smartComponentId)`, scans `objectIndex.sourceComponentId`/`smartComponentId`, and recursively walks `ownedObjectIds`, `objectRoles`, and `childComponentRoles`; it does not use `detachedObjectIds` or `smartComponentConnectionZoneObjectIds`. That local helper drives `currentSmartComponentOnly` filtering at `snap-selection-manager.mjs:126-130`.
  Risk: Snap filtering can disagree with scene visibility, inspector highlighting, store dependency APIs, and detached/zone-managed Smart Component objects. Users may be unable to snap to objects that the rest of the app treats as part of the active component, or vice versa.
  Recommendation: Replace the local snap-selection traversal with `smartComponentObjectIds(project, instance)` from `dependencies.mjs`, plus a small wrapper that resolves `smartComponentId` to the instance.

- F24 Member creation has a parallel `modelDefaults.collections.members` resolver instead of using the canonical effective-object merge rule.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/core/model.mjs:97-111` defines effective object resolution as a deep merge of collection `*` defaults, type defaults, and the stored object. `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/member-factory.mjs:25-55` implements a separate default reader for new members: `typeDefaults` chooses the first matching type key from aliases such as `beam`, `supported-beam`, `supporting-beam`, and `primary-beam`; `projectDefaultMaterial` reads only `members["*"].material`; `defaultProfileId` requires only the chosen type default. `createMemberObject` then sets explicit `profile`, `material`, `rotation`, `cardinalPoint`, display color, BIM name, and fabrication part mark at `member-factory.mjs:171-222`.
  Risk: Newly created members and existing members read through `objectById`/`collectionObjects` can apply different default semantics. Defaults under `members["*"]` other than `material`, nested defaults, and central deep-merge behavior are not inherited by creation unless this factory manually mirrors them.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared member-default/effective-new-object helper or make `createMemberObject` compose the same default merge contract before applying creation-only fields such as id, mark, endpoints, and authoring metadata.

- F25 Member read APIs mix raw stored members and effective/default-merged members behind similar names.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/core/model.mjs:103-118` makes `objectById` return an effective object with `modelDefaults` merged in. `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/members.mjs:51-53` exports `memberById(project, memberId)` as a nullable raw `project.model.members` lookup. `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:90-94` exports another `memberById` that is also raw but throws on missing ids. The public store `member(memberId)` method in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:87-94` validates with the raw store helper and then returns `objectById`, so UI callers using `api.member(...)` see default-merged members. `project-command-store.mjs:492-501` uses raw `memberById` for replacement, while `:1051-1056` uses `objectById` specifically for `rotateMember`.
  Risk: Two call sites can ask for a "member" and receive different shapes depending on whether they imported `api/project/members.memberById`, `project-store-model-helpers.memberById`, or public `store.member`. This can hide missing defaults in rendering/interaction code and make command behavior differ from inspector/public store reads.
  Recommendation: Name the distinction explicitly, for example `storedMemberById` versus `effectiveMemberById`, and route public reads through one effective-object API. Mutation helpers can still request stored objects, but their names should make that bypass visible.

- F26 Object/index collection helpers are duplicated with different missing-collection and cloning behavior.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/objects.mjs:1-19` owns one `MODEL_COLLECTIONS` set, `:55-58` requires `model[collection]` to already exist, and `:96-110` stores the original object reference in the collection and `objectIndex`. `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-model-helpers.mjs:10-13` owns a second collection list/set, `:23-26` creates `model[collection] = {}` when missing, `:46-57` rebuilds patch objectIndex entries independently, and `:111-118` clones objects before storing them. Store helpers add a third accessor layer in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:58-67` plus `setIndexedModelObject` at `:718-725`.
  Risk: Project API, store mutations, and Smart Component patch/runtime code can disagree about whether a missing collection is invalid or should be synthesized, whether inserted objects are cloned, and which collections are valid. That weakens `objectIndex` as the single authoritative model index.
  Recommendation: Export the collection registry and strict/patch-mode collection helpers from one project object module. Smart Component patch code can opt into a clearly named "create missing patch collection" mode, but it should inherit the same collection list and indexing rules.

- F27 Plate-sketch normalization bypasses effective `modelDefaults` and reintroduces required/defaulted plate fields.
  Evidence: `docs/quality/code-removal-log.md:4063-4074` records that plate `thickness`, `normal`, and local axes were removed from schema requirements because they may come from `modelDefaults.collections.plates[type]`. But `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/model-and-placement.mjs:17-25` requires `center`, `normal`, `localAxisY`, and `localAxisZ` on the object passed to `normalizeSketchPlacement`, and `:40-61` requires positive `thickness` on the object passed to `normalizePlate`. Store plate-sketch mutations pass raw stored plates into these helpers via `project-command-store.mjs:516-524` and `project-store-plate-sketch-methods.mjs:26-121`, not effective `objectById` plates. The same creation file hardcodes `material: options.material || "S355"` for `plateFromSketchObject` at `model-and-placement.mjs:104` and default `material = "S355"` for `profileFromSectionSketch` at `:116`, even though sample projects place repeated plate material under `modelDefaults.collections.plates.*.material`.
  Risk: A schema-valid plate that relies on plate defaults can fail plate-sketch edits/normalization, and new plates/profiles can ignore a project's chosen material default. This mirrors the member default split from F24/F25 in the plate-sketch path.
  Recommendation: Make plate-sketch operations normalize against an effective plate view or a shared default resolver, then write only intentional object overrides. Replace hardcoded `S355` fallbacks with the project/material default path or require callers to pass a material explicitly.

- F28 Plate-sketch relation behavior is repeated across assert, diagnostic, rank-analysis, solver, and mutation code instead of coming from one relation operation registry.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/relation-analysis.mjs:82-178` validates relation satisfaction with a long relation-type chain, and `:180-290` repeats the same relation-type chain to emit diagnostic records. The same file builds constraint equations with another relation-type chain at `:331-438`. `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/solver-core.mjs:126-140` and `:488-543` implement relation-type handling again for solving, while `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/relation-mutations.mjs:72-110` implements another relation-type chain to choose solve vertices. `relation-analysis.mjs` also still imports unused names such as `finitePositiveNumber`, `arrayValues`, `sketchConstructionVertices`, `sketchEdges`, `sketchVertices`, `sketchRelationKey`, `normalizePlate`, `normalizeSketchObject`, `edgeById`, `requiredIdPair`, `inferredSketchRelations`, `measuredSketchEdgeAngle`, `pointMoved`, `sketchDimensionMode`, `sketchEdgePoints`, and `withSketchRelations` at `:1-47`, which suggests the module boundary was split but not cleaned.
  Risk: Adding or changing a relation type requires editing several switch/if chains across analysis, diagnostics, rank math, solver behavior, and mutation targeting. It is easy for satisfaction checks, UI health, solver movement, and relation inheritance to drift.
  Recommendation: Introduce one relation-operation registry/spec per relation type that owns target ids, satisfaction residual, diagnostic message, rank equations, solver target choice, and optional solve projection. Then make analysis, solver, preview, and mutation modules call that registry instead of reimplementing relation-type chains.

- F29 Plate-sketch dimension APIs can silently downgrade requested driving dimensions to driven dimensions.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/relation-mutations.mjs:345-367` creates a length relation using the caller's `options.mode`, then if the requested driving relation is redundant and `allowRedundantDriving` is not true, recursively replaces it with `{ mode: "driven" }`. The same policy is repeated for angle dimensions at `:380-408` and point-distance dimensions at `:424-452`. In contrast, the mode-changing APIs intentionally pass `allowRedundantDriving: nextMode === "driving"` at `:369-377`, `:411-421`, and `:455-466`, so "set value as driving" and "set mode to driving" have different persistence rules. Store methods expose the value-setting calls directly at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-plate-sketch-methods.mjs:39-60`, and the inspector calls them with `{ mode: "driving" }` when editing dimension values at `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/contributions/plate-sketch-inspector.mjs:131-152`.
  Risk: A caller can ask the public API to make a dimension driving, receive a successful project update, and later find that the stored relation is driven/reference. This hides a constraint-policy decision inside mutation helpers and makes UI/store callers responsible for noticing a changed relation mode after the fact.
  Recommendation: Make redundancy downgrades explicit in the API result or move the policy into the relation-operation registry proposed in F28. If automatic downgrade is intended, return metadata/diagnostics saying the requested driving dimension was stored as driven; otherwise require callers to opt in by requesting `mode: "driven"` or a named auto-downgrade option.

- F30 Plate-sketch relation inference is both implicit and explicit, with no single policy/provenance layer.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/sketch-geometry-and-relations.mjs:125-140` makes `sketchFromOutline` and `sketchFromRectangle` immediately store inferred relations through `withInferredSketchRelations`; `platePlacementFromThreePoints` creates a rectangle sketch through that same path at `:162-185`. `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/model-and-placement.mjs:81-90` uses `sketchSource` for `addSketch`, and Smart Component semantic builders use `sketchFromOutline`/`sketchFromRectangle` at `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/semantic-builders.mjs:126-135`, so authored/generated sketches can receive inferred constraints without a caller-visible relation step. Topology mutation also infers relations for new edges by default in `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/relation-mutations.mjs:204-227`, while the app separately exposes an explicit `store.inferPlateSketchRelations` command through `api-register.json:727`, store methods at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-plate-sketch-methods.mjs:107-108`, and UI action metadata at `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-editable-object-property-metadata.mjs:265`.
  Risk: The project can persist relations that were inferred automatically, inferred by topology repair, or explicitly requested by the user, but relation records do not expose that provenance. Later normalization/deduplication treats them alike, making it harder to distinguish author intent from convenience constraints when solving, previewing, or cleaning redundant relations.
  Recommendation: Centralize sketch-relation inference policy. Creation/topology APIs should take a documented `inferRelations` policy, and inferred relation records should either carry provenance metadata or be produced only through a named inference operation whose result is visible to callers.

- F31 Direct plate-sketch vertex moves silently remove touching equal-length relations.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/solver-core.mjs:563-569` implements `relaxRelationsForDirectVertexMove` by filtering out `equal-length` relations that touch any changed vertex, then returns a sketch with those relations removed. `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/relation-mutations.mjs:313-342` calls this relaxation unconditionally from `setPlateSketchVertices` before solving moved vertices, and store methods expose vertex movement directly at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-plate-sketch-methods.mjs:27-32`.
  Risk: A user or API caller can move a point and lose equal-length constraints as a side effect, without a result payload that identifies which relations were removed. Other relation types are solved or asserted instead, so relation relaxation policy is hidden and type-specific.
  Recommendation: Move relation relaxation into the relation-operation policy layer from F28 and make mutation APIs return or emit metadata for removed/relaxed constraints. If silent removal is intentional for drag editing, it should be an explicit direct-edit option rather than the default behavior for every vertex update call.

- F32 Plate-sketch topology edits silently prune dependent bends and can change plate type.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/topology.mjs:111-124` computes bend ids whose target edges were removed, adds descendants through `bendDescendantIds`, filters them out, and then sets `type` to `"bent-plate"` only if bends remain, otherwise `"plate"`. The same helper is used by vertex insertion at `:127-152`, vertex removal at `:155-189`, and corner notching at `:192-264`. Store wrappers return only the updated project plus inserted/notch vertex ids where applicable (`bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-plate-sketch-methods.mjs:63-84`), not the removed bend ids or type/fabrication changes.
  Risk: Editing plate topology can delete bend chains and change the object's semantic type as a side effect without caller-visible dependency metadata. UI/automation can report only a successful sketch operation while losing fabrication data tied to removed edges.
  Recommendation: Return mutation metadata for pruned bend ids and type changes, or route topology edits through a shared dependency/mutation-result contract. If automatic bend pruning is required, make it explicit in store/API result payloads and UI status messages.

- F33 Profile catalog APIs keep two live catalog shapes: raw profile map and wrapped `{ profiles }` library pack.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/profiles.mjs:12-15` accepts either a raw profile map or an object with a `.profiles` map. `projectProfileCatalog` then returns a raw merged map at `:28-30`. The source library pack is wrapped (`bobercad/data/libraries/profiles/profile-libraries/starter-profiles/config.json:28`), while store `api.profiles()` returns the raw merged map via `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:288-290`. Normal runtime code still falls back between those shapes, for example `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/member-create-controller.mjs:112-120` tries `api.profiles?.()` and then falls back to the loaded `profiles` object, and inspector code uses `api.profiles?.() || profiles`.
  Risk: Callers cannot tell from the function names whether they should pass a profile library pack, a raw map, or a project-merged map. This preserves a compatibility layer in the core profile API and makes it easier for UI/rendering/runtime paths to accidentally skip project-level profile overrides.
  Recommendation: Split the shapes explicitly, for example `profileMapFromLibraryPack(pack)` and `projectProfileCatalog(project, libraryProfileMap)`, then make public lookup functions accept only the merged raw map. Keep any wrapped-pack adapter at import/load boundaries.

- F34 Trim operation type metadata is duplicated across engine, UI commands, and rendering icons.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/trim-operations.mjs:1` defines the supported trim operation ids as a `Set`. `bobercad/app/ui/commands/trim-operation-metadata.mjs:1-8` repeats the same ids with labels/gap/icons, and `bobercad/app/rendering/trim-operation-icons.mjs:3-10` repeats the same ids and labels again for SVG callout rendering. UI lookup functions fall back to the first local option at `trim-operation-metadata.mjs:10-23`, and rendering lookup functions do the same at `trim-operation-icons.mjs:12-21`.
  Risk: Adding/renaming a trim operation requires synchronized edits in three places. Engine validation can accept a type that UI cannot label/render, or UI/rendering can expose a type the engine rejects.
  Recommendation: Create one trim operation spec registry with ids and engine semantics, then layer UI labels/icons/rendering-only metadata on top of those ids instead of redefining the list.

- F35 Trim operation member references keep scalar and array forms live at the same time.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/trim-operations.mjs:41-50` merges `memberAIds/memberBIds` with legacy scalar `memberAId/memberBId`. Schema allows both scalar and array fields at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:2162-2188`. Store normalization for `profile-cope` writes both arrays and first scalar ids at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:569-578`; non-profile-cope operations reject/delete arrays at `:579-582`. The trim editor also writes both forms when converting/switching operations, for example `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/trim-joint-editor-panel.mjs:933-939` and `:960-969`.
  Risk: `memberAId` can drift from `memberAIds[0]`, and callers must know which operations use scalar-only versus array+scalar. This makes profile-cope a compatibility branch inside every trim operation traversal, validation, UI edit, and evaluator path.
  Recommendation: Choose one canonical shape per trim operation kind. For profile-cope, make arrays canonical and derive scalar first ids only in adapters that still need them, or migrate schema/store/UI to a tagged operation spec where scalar and multi-member operation shapes are separate.

- F36 Work-plane API uses an implicit global-XY fallback as active geometry state.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/work-plane.mjs:9-20` creates a synthetic `"global-xy"` plane from `project.settings.coordinateSystem.origin || [0,0,0]` with fixed axes, and `activeWorkPlane(project, state)` returns it whenever `state.referencePlaneId` is missing at `:47-50`. Creation and interaction controllers call `activeWorkPlane(api.project(), {})` or fall back to it when no custom work plane is set, including work-plane, sketch-create, member-create, plate-create, command-controller, and snap-manager paths.
  Risk: Geometry creation/snapping can proceed on an invented plane that is not stored in `model.referencePlanes`, while explicit reference planes are validated strictly. This is useful UX defaulting, but it keeps a hidden geometry fallback in core project API instead of making the active plane state explicit.
  Recommendation: Treat global XY as a named default work-plane policy in viewer/editor state or project settings, and make callers pass an explicit default-plane request. Keep strict project reference-plane resolution separate from the UI fallback.

- F37 Number formatting is reimplemented across core, rendering, and UI instead of using one formatting contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/core/format.mjs:3-16` defines `formatNumber` with `digits`, `trimTrailingZeros`, and `invalid` options. Rendering annotations define `formatDraftingNumber` with direct `toFixed` in `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/drafting-dimensions.mjs:10-11`; `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/member-transform-panel.mjs:12-23` defines another `finiteInteger` plus `formatNumber`; `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/panel-elements.mjs:24-30` defines `formatControlNumber`; Smart Component parameter values use `formatParameterNumber` in `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/smart-component-parameter-values.mjs:370-371`; inspector metadata has direct `toFixed(3)` formatting in `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-editable-object-property-metadata.mjs:501`, `inspector-property-metadata.mjs:859`, and `inspector-support-object-property-metadata.mjs:134`.
  Risk: Numeric rounding, invalid display, and trailing-zero rules can differ between overlays, forms, inspector rows, Smart Component parameters, and core labels. Users can see different text for the same value depending on the panel.
  Recommendation: Promote `formatNumber` as the shared primitive and add small named presets for control values, drafting dimensions, inspector values, and parameter labels. Local formatters should import those presets instead of reimplementing rounding.

- F38 Feature cutter routing is split between the generic cut-body API and scene-only hole/slot cutters.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/cut-features.mjs:8` classifies `hole-pattern` and `slot-hole` in `NON_CUT_FEATURE_TYPES`, and `cutBodiesForFeature` returns `[]` for those types at `:317` instead of returning cutter bodies. The actual hole/slot subtraction path is implemented separately in `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-feature-cutters.mjs:61-127`, where `holePatternCutters`, `slotCutters`, and `holeOrSlotCut` build cylinders/prisms and call `csgSubtract`.
  Risk: A caller using `cutBodiesForFeature` as the generic feature-to-cutter API gets no bodies for holes or slots, while rendering knows a separate route. Adding a new feature type requires knowing whether it belongs in the generic body pipeline, scene feature cutter pipeline, trim evaluator pipeline, or a silent empty-list bucket.
  Recommendation: Centralize feature-to-cutter routing in one registry/API, or make `cutBodiesForFeature` return an explicit "handled by scene feature cutter" result instead of an indistinguishable empty list for active cut features.

- F39 Fastener catalog access has both strict wrapped and loose raw-map shapes.
  Evidence: The fastener library schema requires a top-level `fasteners` object at `bobercad/app/schemas/fastener-library.schema.json:7-14` and defines entries under `fasteners` at `:71-77`.   Risk: Fastener catalog consumers do not share one contract. A raw-map shape can work in rendering while failing store/Smart Component validation, making catalog bugs environment-dependent.
  Recommendation: Add one shared `fastenerCatalogEntries` helper in a runtime-safe catalog API module and make renderer/store/Smart Component code all use the same strict or explicitly versioned compatibility behavior.

- F40 Feature reference basis resolution is duplicated between fastener rendering and feature cutters.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/evaluators/fastener-evaluator.mjs:58-98` resolves `feature.reference` for `plate-face`, `interfaceRef`, and explicit `origin/normal/localAxisY/localAxisZ`. `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-feature-cutters.mjs:22-58` implements the same three-branch resolver for hole/slot cutters, including plate face offsets, `stationReferenceInterfaceRef`, and interface basis extraction.
  Risk: Fastener axes and hole/slot cutter axes can drift if one resolver adds support for a reference shape, fallback, or validation rule and the other does not. This is a core geometry contract currently owned by two scene/evaluator modules.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared feature-reference basis resolver under `engine/geometry` and have fastener evaluation plus scene feature cutters call it with their own error prefix/metadata needs.

- F41 Trim operation evaluation still falls back from missing/unknown operation types instead of requiring the schema/API contract.
  Evidence: The project schema requires each `trimJointOperation` to include `id`, `type`, and `memberAId` at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:2141-2147`, and enumerates supported types at `:2152-2160`. Store normalization rejects unsupported types through `TRIM_OPERATION_TYPES` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:569-572`. But `evaluateTrimJointOperationFeatures` defaults `const type = operation.type || "end-butt-1"` in `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/evaluators/trim-evaluator.mjs:430-434`, and `evaluateTrimJointOperationMarkerPlanes` repeats the same default at `:532-533`. The marker-plane evaluator also falls through unknown types to a member-A marker plane at `:557` instead of throwing.
  Risk: Invalid or legacy trim operation data can still render/evaluate as an end-butt trim or show a marker plane while schema/store would reject it. That masks data-contract bugs and makes viewer behavior differ from authoring validation.
  Recommendation: Remove the runtime default or move it into a named legacy importer/migration. Evaluators should call the canonical trim operation type validator and throw on missing/unsupported `operation.type`.

- F42 Weld reference dispatch is a catch-all instead of a canonical reference-kind contract.
  Evidence: The weld schema allows `reference.kind` as any string at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:2643-2648`, and `ctx.weld.fillet` stores `data.reference` without validating reference kind in `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/semantic-builders.mjs:494-509`. - F43 Local frame/up-axis fallback policy is implemented independently in member, path, and connection geometry.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/member-evaluator.mjs:123-134` builds member frame `y/z` axes from global up, switching to `[0,1,0]` when the member axis is near vertical. `bobercad/app/engine/api/geometry/paths.mjs:61-68` builds path frames from a preferred up vector, then falls back to `[1,0,0]` and `[0,1,0]`. Connection primitives have their own local-axis policies, for example `secondary-web-context.mjs:69-75` projects support `localAxisZ` then falls back to beam-hole `localAxisZ`, and `dual-member-gusset.mjs:122-126` projects global Z then falls back to main-interface Z.
  Risk: Member frames, generic path frames, fin-plate layout references, and gusset plate axes can choose different local axes around vertical/parallel cases. Near-degenerate geometry may flip or rotate depending on which module authored it.
  Recommendation: Promote a shared frame/basis resolver with named policies (`global-up`, `preferred-up`, `interface-z`, etc.) and make member/path/connection code call it instead of embedding local fallback chains.

- F44 Reference-plane API documentation still advertises `size` although schema/runtime require `extents`.
  Evidence: `ctx.reference.plane` in `bobercad/app/engine/api/api-register.json:303-310` documents data as "origin, normal, axisX, axisY, optional size/extents and metadata".   Risk: Smart Component authors following the API register can provide `size` and hit a runtime builder error, while generated API docs suggest both shapes are valid.

- F45 Trim region geometry silently substitutes a unit profile span when profile data is missing.

- F46 Smart Component interface resolution applies a hardcoded geometry nudge outside the shared member-interface resolver.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:389-414` resolves component interfaces, and the main-role branch modifies the secondary reference point by `secondaryBeamDirection(...) * 10` when `iface.faceRef === "connection-secondary-facing-section-face"` at `:399-407`. - F47 Smart Component source resolution is duplicated and ignores the stored `library`/`version` contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-catalog.mjs:16-42` and `:24-56` define catalog/preset/definition resolution, while `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-registry.mjs:38-43`, `:107-123`, and `:126-147` duplicate the same catalog and instance-source lookup responsibilities. The project schema requires `sourceComponent` to use `librarySource` with `library`, `id`, and `version` at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:2688-2724` and `:3341-3359`, but both resolver paths read only `sourceComponent.id` (`smart-component-catalog.mjs:24-28`, `smart-component-registry.mjs:107-123`). Make registry/store/scripts call that helper, and use a separate preset-id API for transient preset previews instead of constructing partial `sourceComponent` records.

- F48 Smart Component creation splits preset and definition resolution across the caller boundary.
  Evidence: `createProjectSmartComponentFromPreset(project, catalog, presetId, ...)` receives the catalog and resolves the preset in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-creation.mjs:321-323`, but then requires `options.definition` at `:324` instead of deriving the matching definition from the catalog.
