  Risk: A caller can pass a definition that does not match the preset, and the API keeps the id-only `sourceComponent` compatibility path alive. Creation behavior is split between store and Smart Component runtime instead of being owned by one creation contract.
  Recommendation: Make `createProjectSmartComponentFromPreset` resolve the definition through the canonical catalog/source helper. Keep any test-only or preview-only definition override as an explicit, validated override that asserts `definition.type === preset.type`.

- F49 Smart Component connection object creation is implemented twice with separate defaults.
  Evidence: top-level Smart Component creation builds automatic interfaces, a connection zone, and an assembly in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-creation.mjs:198-275`. Nested child-component creation builds the same object family independently in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:289-355`, with separate handling for prewired zone/assembly ids, unsupported legacy fields, interface ids, names, assembly parent/children, and authoring metadata.
  Risk: Top-level and nested connection components can drift in generated object shape, naming, authoring metadata, and supported interface types. Fixes to zone/interface/assembly creation must be remembered in two places.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared connection-object factory for Smart Component runtime that accepts a top-level or nested mode/options object, and make both creation paths use it.

- F50 Smart Component instance input accessors exist, but many callers still read raw `inputs` shapes directly.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-instance-helpers.mjs:7-27` exports accessors for role inputs, `connectionZoneId`, and `assemblyId`. Other code still reads the same fields directly, including `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:71-77`, `:448-462`, `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-helpers.mjs:130-134`, `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-creation.mjs:414`, and `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/smart-component-preview-service.mjs:256-261`.
  Risk: Required vs optional behavior, empty-string handling, and fallback member-id logic can diverge between runtime build, store mutations, preview filtering, and inspector/display code.
  Recommendation: Promote this helper module into the canonical Smart Component input accessor surface, add any missing permissive/read-only helpers needed by UI preview, and migrate store/runtime callers off raw `inputs.*` reads where validation or null semantics matter.

- F51 `setSmartComponentRoleActive` has a runtime implementation but the store reimplements it with different validation.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-options.mjs:103-109` exports `setSmartComponentRoleActive` and validates against `instance.objectRoles`. The store imports/runtime-wraps `setSmartComponentPlateIncluded` but not `setSmartComponentRoleActive` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:50-57`, and `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:394-400` reimplements role toggling by validating `definition.components` and writing `smartComponent.suppressedRoles = setRoleInList(...)`.
  Risk: Runtime and store role toggles can disagree when a role exists in `definition.components` but not in `objectRoles`, or vice versa. Future changes to role suppression semantics must be made twice.
  Recommendation: Make the store commit through the runtime `setSmartComponentRoleActive` path, or move the shared role validation/toggle function behind one helper used by both runtime and store wrappers.

- F52 Smart Component outputs use suffix-based validation instead of a declared output contract.
  Evidence: `ctx.output` calls `outputContractIssue` in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-build.mjs:182-190`; `outputContractIssue` only validates keys ending in `Ids` or `Id` in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-overrides.mjs:145-157`. `setNestedOutput` accepts any non-empty dot path and creates nested objects at `smart-component-overrides.mjs:130-143`, while project schema stores `smartComponentInstance.outputs` as an open object with `additionalProperties: true` at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:2771-2774`.
  Risk: Component outputs become an implicit naming convention rather than a typed API. Misspelled output names, non-id payloads, or changed shapes can be consumed by child components/UI without schema-level or definition-level guarantees.
  Recommendation: Add a declared output contract to Smart Component definitions and validate `ctx.output` against it. Keep the `Id`/`Ids` suffix rule only as a temporary lint/backstop, not the primary contract.

- F53 Runtime Smart Component definition validation is weaker than the JSON schema contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/schemas/smart-component.schema.json:7-18` requires `$schema`, `type`, `kind`, `title`, `version`, `presets`, `parameters`, `components`, and `ui`, and the top-level schema has `additionalProperties: false` at `:130`. Runtime `defineSmartComponent` in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-parameters-and-definition.mjs:270-292` requires most semantic fields but does not require `$schema` and does not reject unknown top-level keys. It only applies known-key checks to selected nested objects such as interfaces, components, and previews.
  Risk: Smart Component configs loaded as JS/runtime objects can contain typo fields or unsupported top-level contract drift that would fail schema validation but pass runtime loading. Schema and runtime can stop describing the same component definition language.
  Recommendation: Make runtime definition loading validate against the same schema or mirror the schema's top-level known-key set, including `$schema` policy. If JS-only fields such as `build` are allowed, isolate them as runtime-only extensions with an explicit allowlist.

- F54 Smart Component preview context ids are only strictly validated in a contract script, while runtime silently ignores unknown ids.
  Evidence: `smartComponentPreviewContextsForPreset` reads preset preview contexts in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-preview-contexts.mjs:20-24`, and `orderContexts` drops unknown ids with `.find(...).filter(Boolean)` before appending all remaining default contexts at `:34-39`. `defineSmartComponent` validates preview context entries only as non-empty unique strings in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-parameters-and-definition.mjs:245-259`. A contract script separately checks known context ids for connection presets at `scripts/contracts/smart_component_lifecycle_contracts.js:140-153`.
  Risk: A typo in `preview.contexts` can silently fall back to unrelated default preview contexts at runtime, especially outside the contract-covered connection preset path. Preview availability can look valid while not testing the intended sample scene.
  Recommendation: Move known-context validation into runtime definition loading or share the preview-context registry with `defineSmartComponent`, and make unknown context ids fail at catalog load time.

- F55 Smart Component catalog loading is not concurrency-safe.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-registry.mjs:5-7` keeps global `definitions`, `presets`, and a `loaded` boolean. `loadSmartComponentDefinitions` returns early only after `loaded` is true (`:82-83`), but it does not store an in-flight promise before awaiting JSON/module loads at `:85-100`. Registration rejects duplicates in `registerSmartComponentDefinition` at `:52-67`.
  Risk: Two concurrent callers before the first load completes can both load the register and attempt to register the same definitions/presets, causing a duplicate-definition or duplicate-preset failure. The API looks idempotent but is only safe after the first call has fully completed.
  Recommendation: Replace the bare boolean with a cached `loadPromise` that is assigned before async work starts; subsequent callers should await that promise. Keep `loaded` only as derived state if still useful.

- F56 Id sanitization is split between Smart Component `safeId` and the project object API `cleanId`.
  Evidence: `safeId` in `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-runtime-validation.mjs:78-82` replaces every non-alphanumeric character with `_` and strips leading/trailing underscores. The general project object API `cleanId` in `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/objects.mjs:61-67` preserves `:`, `-`, and `_`, and strips repeated edge underscores with a different regex. Smart Component creation/build use `safeId` for generated ids in `smart-component-creation.mjs:302-305` and `smart-component-build.mjs:318`.
  Risk: Generated ids differ depending on whether an object is created through Smart Component runtime or the public project object API. Hyphenated component types such as `stair-system` become `stair_system` through one path but can remain hyphenated through another.
  Recommendation: Put id sanitization in one project id helper and make Smart Component generation call it with an explicit mode if it needs stricter ids.

- F57 Smart Component diagnostic display is implemented both in runtime overrides and the project store.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/modules/smart-components/smart-component-overrides.mjs:16-20` defines `DIAGNOSTIC_DISPLAY` and `addDiagnosticDisplay` applies it to plates, fastener groups, welds, features, and trim joints at `:48-56`. `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:148-152` defines the same display object locally, and `markSmartComponentError` applies it over the same collection list at `:351-366`.
  Risk: Error display styling and eligible object collections can drift between normal Smart Component build diagnostics and store-side reconciliation diagnostics. A future display contract change would need to be remembered in two unrelated files.
  Recommendation: Export one diagnostic display/apply helper from the Smart Component runtime layer and make the store call that helper when it has to mark reconciliation errors.

- F58 Smart Component store reconciliation performs hidden geometry repair after generation.
  Evidence: `fitMemberEndToTrimPlane` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:367-407` finds a generated trim plane, resolves the secondary member interface, intersects the member axis with the plane, and mutates the member `start` or `end` point. `reconcileGeneratedSmartComponents` then runs generated Smart Components through up to four regenerate/fit iterations and one final regenerate at `:408-420`.
  Risk: Smart Component build output is not fully authoritative; endpoint geometry can be silently changed by a store-only post-process that is not part of the Smart Component definition, primitive API, or member/trim API. Other code paths that call runtime helpers directly can miss this repair loop, and the fixed iteration count is another hidden fallback policy.
  Recommendation: Move the beam-to-trim fitting into the relevant Smart Component/connection primitive or expose it as an explicit model operation/solver result. The store should commit the result, not own geometry repair logic.

- F59 Regenerated Smart Component commands can under-report changed objects.
  Evidence: `deriveProjectCommandObjectIds` short-circuits diffing whenever explicit metadata is present in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-registry.mjs:28-40`. `commitRegeneratedSmartComponent` passes only `changedObjectIds: [smartComponentId]` and `regeneratedObjectIds: [smartComponentId]` after `reconcileGeneratedSmartComponents(regenerateSmartComponent(...))` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:422-428`. `resolveSmartComponentDiagnostics` does the same at `:488-489`. Store Smart Component creation/update paths repeat the pattern: `createSmartComponentFromPreset` reports only the created instance at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:299-310`, `updateSmartComponent` reports only the instance at `:413-423`, and `setSmartComponentConnectionMember` reports only the instance plus member ids at `:470-481`, while reconciliation can also mutate generated members, trim joints, plates, features, fastener groups, welds, zones, interfaces, and helper objects.
  Risk: Subscribers or render/update paths that trust command result ids can miss objects actually changed by regeneration. The fallback diff code exists but is bypassed by the explicit, too-small metadata list.
  Recommendation: Either let the command registry derive ids for regeneration commands, or have Smart Component patch/reconcile return the full touched-id set and pass that complete set through command metadata.

- F60 Store interface validation is weaker than `project.schema.json`.
  Evidence: `validateInterface` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:441-455` checks supported `type`, owner id, optional string fields, optional `memberEnd`, optional vectors, and extents, but it does not enforce schema conditional requirements. `project.schema.json` requires `memberEnd` for `member-end-face`, requires `faceRef: "web-center-plane"` for `member-web`, requires `faceRef` for `planar-face`, requires origin/normal/local axes for `plate-face`, constrains `stationReference` and `faceRef` enums, and disallows unknown properties at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:1207-1378`.
  Risk: Store update paths can accept interface objects that later fail schema validation or behave differently in geometry resolution. The store validator becomes a parallel, less strict interface contract.
  Recommendation: Replace manual interface validation with schema-backed validation or move the schema's conditional interface contract into one shared model validator used by both store and JSON checks.

- F61 Store default-generation policies are hardcoded instead of centralized.
  Evidence: `defaultGridAxis` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-model-helpers.mjs:299-315` derives missing grid-axis spacing from the previous two axes or hardcodes `6000`, then generates numeric/letter labels. `createGridSystem` hardcodes another initial grid default with two x axes and two y axes at positions `0` and `6000` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:341-357`. `defaultTrimJointParticipant` chooses the nearest member end from a computed reference point at `project-store-model-helpers.mjs:500-507`. `defaultTrimJointOperation` chooses member A/B from participant order, sets `enabled: true`, and defaults ids to `end_butt_1_${index}` regardless of operation type at `:623-645`.
  Risk: UI/store-created model objects can get defaults that are not visible in schemas, model defaults, command metadata, or API registers. Scripts or future APIs that create the same object family may choose different spacing, labels, member roles, or ids.
  Recommendation: Extract grid-axis and trim-operation default policies into named project/model API helpers with documented inputs. If these are UI convenience defaults, keep them out of generic store helpers and call them explicitly from UI-facing commands.

- F62 Smart Component deletion keeps a fallback removal algorithm that is weaker than the canonical helper.
  Evidence: `deleteSmartComponent` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs:367-383` uses injected `smartComponentRemovalObjectIds` when it is a function, but otherwise falls back to a local list of `smartComponentObjectIds`, owned ids, generated helper ids, and the instance id. The canonical helper in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:262-270` also includes `smartComponentConnectionHelperObjectIds`, which collects connection zones and interfaces tied to the instance at `:242-261`.
  Risk: Alternate/test construction of `createSmartComponentStoreMethods` without the injected helper can leave connection helper objects behind. The fallback makes deletion semantics depend on dependency injection shape rather than one required API.
  Recommendation: Remove the fallback and require `smartComponentRemovalObjectIds`, or export one canonical removal-id helper that both command store and Smart Component store methods must call.

- F63 Datum/grid creation methods are misplaced inside the Smart Component store-method module.
  Evidence: `createSmartComponentStoreMethods` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-smart-component-methods.mjs` returns `createLevel(options = {})` at `:315-332` and `createGridSystem(options = {})` at `:334-365`. These functions create generic `levels` and `gridSystems`, validate them, add them to the project, and update grid level ids; they are not Smart Component-specific.
  Risk: Project datum/grid authoring is hidden behind a Smart Component method bundle, making module ownership misleading and increasing the chance that future datum/grid defaults, validation, or UI commands get coupled to Smart Component dependencies.
  Recommendation: Move level/grid creation into a dedicated project datum/grid store module or into the central project command store next to other generic project object creation methods.

- F64 Trim joint store methods validate operations but not the top-level trim-joint schema contract.
  Evidence: `replaceTrimJoint` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:628-635` validates only that the update returns an object with the same id. `updateTrimJoint` in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-trim-methods.mjs:66-71` blocks id/type/jointPoint changes but then merges arbitrary patch fields without a top-level trim-joint validator. `removeTrimJointParticipant` can filter operations to an empty array at `project-store-trim-methods.mjs:104-113`, and `removeTrimJointOperation` can remove the last operation at `:171-175`. `project.schema.json` requires `trimJoint.operations` with `minItems: 1` and disallows unknown top-level trim-joint properties at `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:2465-2522`.
  Risk: Store commands can create or update trim joints that pass local operation-level checks but fail project schema validation. This is another parallel, weaker model contract.
  Recommendation: Add a top-level `validateTrimJoint` helper that enforces schema-level required fields, operation count, participant count, and known keys, and call it from `replaceTrimJoint` and create/update/remove trim paths.

- F65 Dimension annotations have their own Smart Component role/interface/parameter resolution layer.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/dimension-geometry-and-label-context.mjs:36-53` reads `smartComponent.objectRoles`, `project.objectIndex`, `project.model.connectionZones`, `smartComponent.inputs.connectionZoneId`, definition interface order, and `smartComponent.referenceParameters` directly. `interfaceByRole` and `rawInterfaceByRole` repeat interface lookup at `:523-530`. The index-based interface mapping uses `definition.interfaces` index to read `zone.interfaceIds[index]` at `:45-48`.
  Risk: Dimension overlays can resolve a different role, interface, or parameter value than Smart Component runtime/build context if role values become arrays, interface order changes, connection zone ids move, or default/reference parameter semantics change. This keeps another bypass around the canonical Smart Component accessors.
  Recommendation: Expose a read-only Smart Component annotation context/helper from runtime that resolves role objects, role interfaces, and parameter values once, and make dimension annotations consume that instead of manually walking project/model shapes.

- F66 Hole diameter annotation text contains an encoding artifact.
  Evidence: `draftingText` in `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/dimension-geometry-and-label-context.mjs:70-73` returns a mojibake two-character diameter prefix for `spec.reference.kind === "hole-diameter"`.
  Risk: Hole diameter dimensions can display corrupted text instead of the intended diameter symbol/prefix.
  Recommendation: Normalize annotation text encoding and use a tested UTF-8 diameter symbol or an ASCII-safe product-approved prefix.

- F67 Hole pattern annotation falls back to hardcoded `bolts.rows`/`bolts.columns` parameter paths.
  Evidence: `holePatternDimension` in `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/dimensions/hole-pattern.mjs:11-16` uses `spec.reference.rowsParameter || "bolts.rows"` and `spec.reference.columnsParameter || "bolts.columns"`, then falls back from parameter values to generated row/column counts.
  Risk: A dimension spec missing explicit row/column paths can still render and edit against bolt-specific paths, which couples a generic hole-pattern handler to one component parameter naming convention. It can hide incomplete dimension specs during component authoring.
  Recommendation: Require `rowsParameter` and `columnsParameter` in dimension specs for editable pattern count annotations, or move the bolt-path default into a named component-level preset before the generic handler runs.

- F68 Annotation perpendicular-axis helpers are duplicated between drafting and dimension context modules.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/drafting-dimensions.mjs:17-28` exports `perpendicularAxis` and `perpendicularDimensionOffset`. `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/dimension-geometry-and-label-context.mjs:162-173` redefines local `perpendicularAxis` and `perpendicularDimensionOffset` with the same roles instead of importing the exported drafting helpers.
  Risk: Tolerance behavior and fallback marker-axis selection can drift between generated dimension lines and higher-level dimension context calculations.
  Recommendation: Import the exported drafting helpers into the dimension context, or move them into one annotation geometry helper used by both files.

- F69 Member-create interaction reimplements member profile/default fallback outside the creation API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/member-create-controller.mjs:112-180` owns a local profile resolver: `profileCatalog` tries `api.profiles?.()` and falls back to the loaded `profiles` object; `profileFromDefaults` repeats the member-default preferred-key policy and adds an extra "any default key containing type" pass; `profileFromExistingMember` can use the first existing member profile; `profileFromCatalog` can use the first catalog id; `memberOptionsFor` injects that profile into preview/create options. The canonical factory path in `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/member-factory.mjs:52-55` requires a profile from the type default when `options.profile` is absent, and `createMemberObject` applies it at `:172-174`.
  Risk: Viewer member creation can mask a missing required type default by supplying an existing-member or first-catalog profile, while non-viewer callers using the same public creation API fail. The UI also has a different default precedence than `member-factory`, and its startup catalog fallback can skip project-level profile overrides already exposed through `api.profiles()`.
  Recommendation: Move the effective member-creation profile/default resolver into the project API/store layer, return explicit diagnostics when the project lacks required defaults, and let the interaction controller either call that resolver or pass only a user-selected profile.

- F70 Member transform commits are assembled in the interaction controller instead of one store transaction/API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/member-transform-edit-controller.mjs:971-1004` commits a single drag/edit by calling `api.moveMemberWithLayout` or `api.updateMember` with `{ regenerateSmartComponents: false }`, optionally calling `api.upsertRelation` or `api.deleteRelation`, then requiring `api.regenerateMemberSmartComponents`, recomputing affected ids through `affectedObjectIdsForMemberChange`, and applying a local project patch. The store already has separate public methods for `draftMemberProject`, member update/move, relation update/delete, and regeneration at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:829-862`, `:1075-1101`; `api-register.json:689-697` exposes only a non-mutating draft API, not a single transform transaction.
  Risk: One user-visible transform can become multiple store commits with controller-owned ordering, relation side effects, regeneration timing, affected-object calculation, and local preview rollback. Undo/history, changed/regenerated object metadata, and Smart Component regeneration behavior can drift from other member update paths.
  Recommendation: Add a store-level member transform operation/transaction that accepts the member operation plus relation intent and returns the committed project with changed/regenerated/removed ids. Reuse the same operation for live draft generation so preview and commit share one sequencing policy.

- F71 Member-edit tuning settings are read from `authoringSettings` but exist only as code fallbacks.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/member-transform-edit-controller.mjs:211-219` reads `smartRebuildDelayMs`, `memberEditDragSnapRadius`, and `memberEditDragSnapMaxIntervalMs` with hardcoded fallbacks `500`, `6000`, and `80`; `:670` reads `relationConflictTolerance` with fallback `1`; `localSnapOptions` hardcodes large-project thresholds and candidate caps at `:50-66`; drag snap context adds more hardcoded caps at `:568-579` and throttling thresholds at `:592-612`. `rg` finds those setting names only in this controller, while `viewer-settings.schema.json:530-533` sets `authoring.additionalProperties` to `false`, so they cannot be added to validated viewer settings. The actual `viewer-settings.json:147-285` includes related authoring/manipulator settings but not these fields.
  Risk: Performance, snapping, Smart Component rebuild delay, and relation conflict tolerance appear configurable from the code shape, but are effectively hidden constants. Operators cannot tune them through the authoritative settings file, and future cleanup may remove or rename them without schema/test visibility.
  Recommendation: Either add the intended fields to `viewer-settings.json` and `viewer-settings.schema.json`, or stop reading them as settings and move the constants into a named member-edit policy module with tests.

- F72 Plate bend creation owns bend ids and default bend parameters in the UI controller instead of the project API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-bend-controller.mjs:6-25` builds bend ids locally from target edge strings using a private regex sanitizer, and `:72-80` hardcodes direction selection plus `angle: 90`, `flangeLength: 80`, radius `Math.max(plate.thickness || 8, 8)`, and round auto relief. The project bend API is strict validation/upsert only: `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/bend-normalization.mjs:6-35` requires id, angle, radius, flangeLength, direction, and relief; `bends.mjs:6-36` only normalizes and replaces same-target bends. Inspector editing has its own display fallback for relief radius at `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-editable-object-property-metadata.mjs:288-290`.
  Risk: Any other caller that wants to create a bend must rediscover the UI controller's id/default policy or hand-author every field. Bend ids also use a third local sanitization rule, reinforcing the broader id-policy split from F56.
  Recommendation: Move target-to-bend-id and default bend construction into the project bend API, for example `createPlateBendForTarget(plate, target, options)`, and let the UI controller pass only target/direction/user overrides.

- F73 Manual plate creation has UI-local defaults instead of inheriting project plate defaults.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-create-controller.mjs:11-14` defines default preview dimensions and axis-lock mode; `:69-87` reads `authoringSettings.defaultPlateDepth`/`defaultPlateWidth` even though those keys are absent from `viewer-settings.json` and `viewer-settings.schema.json`; preview construction hardcodes `id: "manual_plate_preview"`, `material: "S355"`, and `thickness: 8` at `:247-260`; final creation hardcodes `id: "manual_plate"`, `type: "plate"`, `material: "S355"`, `thickness: 8`, `placementIntent`, and display colors before calling `api.createPlate` at `:430-444`. The store create path delegates to `addPlateObject`/`normalizePlate` (`project-command-store.mjs:789-793`), while `normalizePlate` requires explicit positive thickness and does not resolve defaults (`model-and-placement.mjs:40-72`); F27 already tracks the same default split in plate-sketch APIs.
  Risk: A manually created plate ignores `modelDefaults.collections.plates` and material defaults by writing explicit S355/8 mm overrides from the UI path. Preview can also diverge from future store/default behavior because it manually constructs a plate-like object instead of asking the plate API for an effective draft.
  Recommendation: Add a project API/store helper for manual plate creation and preview drafting that resolves project defaults once. The controller should pass points, work-plane/placement intent, and user overrides, not default material/thickness/id policy.

- F74 Plate-sketch dimension overlay reads styling settings that are not in the viewer settings contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/dimension-overlay.mjs:80-88` reads `plateSketchDimensionOffset`, `plateSketchCleanDimensionTickSize`, `plateSketchCleanDimensionExtensionOvershoot`, `plateSketchCleanDimensionLabelOffset`, `plateSketchCleanDimensionLineWidth`, `plateSketchCleanDimensionColor`, `plateSketchDimensionColor`, `plateSketchDrivenDimensionColor`, and `plateSketchReferenceDimensionColor`, with hardcoded fallbacks. `rg` finds these setting keys only in this module, not in `viewer-settings.json` or `viewer-settings.schema.json`; the schema sets `authoring.additionalProperties` to `false` at `viewer-settings.schema.json:530-533`.
  Risk: Dimension overlay style appears configurable to the renderer but is not represented in the authoritative settings file/schema, so changes must be made in code and cannot be validated or customized consistently with other viewer settings.
  Recommendation: Add these fields to the viewer settings schema/config if they are intended runtime settings, or move them into named rendering constants so they are not pseudo-settings.

- F75 Plate-sketch dimension edit/toggle workflow is duplicated between the overlay drag actions and the inspector panel.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-dimensions.mjs:31-83` has three separate prompt/parse/default paths for length, angle, and point distance, and `:85-180` applies the same three dimension value APIs with `{ mode: "driving" }`, then re-reads the relation and emits redundant-as-reference messages. `:195-235` independently resolves a relation from the updated project and toggles length/angle/distance mode through type-specific APIs. The inspector has a second dispatch surface over the same relation value APIs at `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/contributions/plate-sketch-inspector.mjs:131-152`, a second mode toggle dispatch at `:160-183`, a separate redundant/conflicted relation resolution path at `:365-405`, and separate driving/reference actions at `:491-518`.
  Risk: Double-click overlay editing and inspector editing can diverge on numeric parsing, default rounding, selected-relation recovery after mutation, redundant relation messaging, and driving/reference behavior. The core API already owns downgrade policy for redundant driving dimensions (F29), but the UI still repeats action orchestration in two places.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared plate-sketch dimension action service for UI callers. It should own value parsing/default formatting, relation lookup after mutation, type-specific value/mode dispatch, and redundant/conflicted status mapping, while both overlay handles and inspector rows call the same service.

- F76 Feature-body sketch editing is a parallel mutation adapter outside the normal plate-sketch store API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-mutations.mjs:21-32` creates feature-specific patch/update helpers that run plate-sketch data functions on `featureTarget.plate` and commit through `api.setFeatureBody`. Every sketch mutation then branches on `currentTarget.collection === "features"` and either uses the data-layer function plus `api.setFeatureBody` or calls the normal store API (`:35-165`). The normal store methods are centralized in `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-store-plate-sketch-methods.mjs:27-121`, while `setFeatureBody` is a generic body merge for boolean-part features at `bobercad/app/engine/store/project-command-store.mjs:1000-1007`. `featureBodySketchPatch` separately converts the next plate sketch back to feature body shape in `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-targets.mjs:79-93`.
  Risk: Plate sketch edits and feature-body sketch edits share data functions but not one public mutation/result contract. Insert/notch operations can return result metadata for normal plates and feature bodies through separate wrapper code, while side effects from F31/F32 are still reported only through whatever this adapter chooses to preserve. Future plate-sketch API changes must be mirrored in this rendering adapter to keep feature editing working.
  Recommendation: Add a project/store "sketch host" mutation API that accepts a plate object, sketch object, or feature-body target and returns one normalized mutation result. Rendering should call that host API instead of manually branching between plate store methods and feature body patches.

- F77 Plate-sketch overlay styling and hit-target controls are pseudo-settings outside the viewer settings contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-overlays.mjs:37-39`, `:71`, `:92`, `:103-108`, `:129-133`, `:155`, `:173`, `:262-287`, `:310`, and `:412` read `plateSketchCleanOutlineColor`, `plateSketchCleanOutlineLineWidth`, `plateSketchCleanFillColor`, `plateSketchCleanFillOpacity`, `plateSketchSelectedRelationLineWidth`, `plateSketchConstructionEdgeColor`, `plateSketchCenterHandleColor`, `plateSketchCenterHandleOpacity`, `plateSketchCenterHitTolerancePx`, `plateSketchCenterPickPriority`, `plateSketchVertexPickPriority`, `plateSketchConstructionVertexColor`, `plateSketchEdgeHandleColor`, `plateSketchEdgeHitTolerancePx`, `plateSketchInsertPointColor`, `plateSketchInsertPointHoverColor`, `plateSketchInsertPointOpacity`, `plateSketchInsertPointHoverOpacity`, `plateSketchInsertPointRadiusPx`, `plateSketchInsertPointHoverGrowPx`, `plateSketchInsertPointHitTolerancePx`, and `plateSketchRelationActionColor`, all with code fallbacks. `rg` finds these keys only in `drag-edit-overlays.mjs`, not in `viewer-settings.json` or `viewer-settings.schema.json`; the authoring schema disallows additional properties.
  Risk: The overlay looks configurable from code, but the authoritative settings contract cannot provide or validate those fields. This creates hidden UI tuning constants and splits plate-sketch styling between real settings, package constants, and pseudo-settings.
  Recommendation: Either add the intended overlay fields to `viewer-settings.json` and the schema, or move them into a named plate-sketch overlay style policy/constants module and stop reading them as runtime settings.

- F78 Plate-sketch snap logic creates persisted relation patches in the rendering layer.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-snap.mjs:54-66` adds a `collinear` relation candidate while preparing edge-drag snaps; `:372-381` creates `equal-length` relation candidates; `:384-393` creates horizontal/vertical relation candidates; `:419-458` creates coincident, axis, equal-length, and perpendicular relation candidates from vertex drag context. Snap results pass those relation patches back through `:153`, `:234`, and `:475`. The controller then persists them through `applySnapRelations`/`upsertSketchRelation` at `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch-drag-edit-controller.mjs:872-895` and `:1047-1051`.
  Risk: Drag snapping can author constraints from rendering heuristics, outside the project relation inference policy tracked in F30 and outside the relation-operation registry proposed in F28. Relation provenance is still just a normal stored relation, so later solver/inspector flows cannot tell whether it was explicit, inferred, topology-generated, or snap-generated.
  Recommendation: Move snap relation suggestion into a project/API relation policy layer or return explicit provenance metadata for snap-generated relations. Rendering can still request candidates, but the relation patch/spec should come from the same relation operation registry as solver, preview, and inference.

- F79 Plate-sketch edit thresholds are read as settings but are not in the settings contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-snap.mjs:84` and `:209` read `settings.plateSketchMinEdgeLength ?? 1` to block edge/vertex drags before outline collapse. `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch-drag-edit-controller.mjs:959` reads `settings.plateSketchInsertDragThresholdPx ?? DEFAULT_INSERT_VERTEX_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX` to decide when insert-point dragging starts. `rg` finds both setting names only in these implementation files, not in `viewer-settings.json` or `viewer-settings.schema.json`; the authoring settings schema rejects additional properties.
  Risk: Geometry/edit thresholds look configurable but cannot be set or validated through `viewer-settings.json`. If they are invariants, they should be named policy constants; if they are tunable, they belong in the schema.
  Recommendation: Promote these thresholds to validated authoring settings or move them to a named plate-sketch edit policy module with tests around edge-collapse and insert-drag behavior.

- F80 Editing a box feature-body sketch silently converts the feature body to polygonal-prism.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-targets.mjs:23-29` accepts both `polygonal-prism` and `box` bodies as sketchable outlines. `featureBodySketchPlate` maps either shape into a plate-like sketch target at `:31-58`. But `featureBodySketchPatch` returns `{ type: "polygonal-prism", center, axisX, axisY, axisZ, depth, outline }` whenever the original body type is `"box"` at `:79-91`; that patch is committed by the feature mutation adapter through `api.setFeatureBody` (F76).
  Risk: A user can edit a rectangular box cutter through the sketch editor and lose the parametric `box` body shape without an explicit conversion result or warning. Downstream feature editors and schemas must then handle the object as a polygonal prism, even if the edit was only a small rectangular move.
  Recommendation: Route feature-body sketch edits through a feature body API that returns conversion metadata, or require an explicit "convert box to polygonal prism" operation before arbitrary outline editing. If silent conversion is intended, surface it in the UI/status and mutation result.

- F81 Plate-sketch relation action patch mapping is duplicated between the overlay helper and the controller.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-geometry.mjs:161-185` defines `relationPatchFromActionData(type, options = {})` for horizontal/vertical, point, symmetric, fixed, edge-pair, angle, and distance relation patches. `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch-drag-edit-controller.mjs:409-443` defines a second `relationPatchFromAction(handle)` with the same relation type dispatch, plus local prompt handling for angle/distance. The overlay builds matching handle payloads in `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-sketch/drag-edit-overlays.mjs:419-461` and action lists at `:492-573`.
  Risk: Adding/changing a relation action requires keeping the overlay handle shape, preview patch builder, and controller commit patch builder in sync. A relation can preview correctly but commit differently, or vice versa.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared relation action spec/service that builds preview and commit patches from one table and supplies prompt requirements for value-based relations.

- F82 Reference-plane editor keeps `size` and invented extents fallbacks despite the extents-only contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/reference-plane-edit-controller.mjs:19-30` uses `plane.extents` when valid, otherwise derives extents from legacy/alternate `plane.size`, otherwise falls back to `DEFAULT_EXTENTS` from `:4`. In contrast, `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/reference-plane.mjs:49-50` rejects `referencePlane.size` and requires `extents`, and `bobercad/app/engine/api/model/semantic-builders.mjs:144-146` rejects `size` in semantic reference plane creation.
  Risk: Invalid or old reference-plane data can still be displayed and edited in the interaction overlay with invented extents instead of surfacing validation failure. Editing writes an `extents` patch but does not explicitly remove `size`, so mixed-shape data can persist.
  Recommendation: Remove runtime `size`/default-extents fallback from the editor once migrations are complete, or move it into an explicit one-time migration/import path. The editor should require contract-valid `extents`.

- F83 Pick-face identity uses multiple member/object aliases instead of one canonical target DTO.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/selection-controller.mjs:4-7` resolves member picks through `face.collection === "members" ? face.objectId : face.memberId || face.ownerMemberId`. `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-visibility-policy.mjs` also accounts for `face.objectId`, `face.memberId`, and `face.ownerMemberId`; `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs` chooses `face.objectId || context.visibleHit?.objectId || face.memberId || face.ownerMemberId`; and `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-member-geometry-adapters.mjs` emits `ownerMemberId`.
  Risk: Selection, snapping, visibility, and scene metadata must all remember the same alias set. New face producers can choose the wrong field and still partly work in some consumers, making picker behavior dependent on consumer-specific fallback order.
  Recommendation: Define one pick-face target DTO, for example `{ collection, objectId, subId, ownerId }`, migrate producers to emit it, and keep any alias migration in one adapter before selection/snap code sees it.

- F84 Manual sketch creation hardcodes project object defaults in the rendering controller.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/sketch-create-controller.mjs:74-91` calls `api.createSketch` with a hardcoded base id `"manual_sketch"`, `placementIntent` role/source, and display colors. The central project API path exists, but `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/model-and-placement.mjs:81-91` mostly normalizes the object it is given and only supplies a generic `"sketch"` id default when no id is provided.
  Risk: Manual sketch objects can diverge from other sketch creation paths because UI owns semantic defaults that should be a shared project-level draft/factory policy. Display defaults, provenance, and id-prefix behavior must be rediscovered by every future sketch creator.
  Recommendation: Add a project/API helper for manual sketch drafts or sketch creation defaults, then let the interaction controller submit only captured points/work-plane context.

- F85 Snap providers actively emit hybrid old/new candidate DTOs.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:113-124`, `:127-140`, and `:143-171` push flat fields such as `kind`, `point`, `a`, `b`, `priority`, `providerId`, and `target`, then spread the newer `candidateContract(...)` result with `geometry`, `identity`, `visibility`, `ranking`, `reference`, `hints`, and `preview`. Other sources such as `activeReferenceAxes` and `worldAxisCandidate` return only flat candidate fields at `:1235-1290`.
  Risk: The canonical snap-candidate contract is not authoritative at provider boundaries; the solver compatibility layer from F14 remains required because current providers still depend on mixed shapes.
  Recommendation: Make provider helper functions return one canonical DTO shape, or introduce a named provider-adapter step and prohibit direct flat candidate emission outside it.

- F86 Reference-plane snap provider invents axes/spans outside the strict reference-plane contract.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:582-594` fills missing extents with a fallback span, `:598` defaults that span to `5000`, and `:601-603` silently normalizes missing/invalid axes to global X/Y. Corners are emitted only when at least one extent number exists at `:613-624`, while axis snap lines still use fallback spans at `:635-649`.
  Risk: Invalid or partial reference-plane data can still produce snap axes, even though other reference-plane APIs reject missing extents or `size`-style data. This reinforces F82 from a different runtime path.
  Recommendation: Route reference-plane snapping through the same strict reference-plane evaluator used by geometry/API validation, and keep any missing-extents migration outside normal snapping.

- F87 Snap provider registry is incomplete; construction providers are appended outside it.
  Evidence: `SNAP_CANDIDATE_PROVIDERS` declares model/global/active-sketch/adaptive-grid providers at `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:1293-1360`, and `collectRegisteredSnapProviders` runs only that list at `:1362-1364`. `collectSnapCandidates` then separately appends member-create axes, member-edit axes, active-reference axes, `context.constructionAxes`, `context.dragGuideAxes`, and composite candidates at `:1385-1399`.
  Risk: Provider capability/budget metadata is not the full provider surface. New construction-guide behavior can bypass registry-level policy, diagnostics, and future provider-level configuration.
  Recommendation: Register construction, active-reference, drag-guide, and composite providers in the same provider table or move the table out of this file if it is only documentation.

- F88 Snap tuning defaults are split across manager, provider, controller context, and settings.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-manager.mjs:108-129` invents auto-search radius plus default member/plate candidate limits; `:143-151` clamps intersection and visible candidate budgets. `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:552`, `:598`, `:941-942`, `:1183`, `:1215`, and `:1378-1381` define separate level/reference/global span and candidate defaults. `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-settings.json:244` exposes `globalAxisSnapSpan`, but no corresponding `levelSnapSpan` or `referencePlaneSnapSpan`.
  Risk: Snap performance and visible guide size are tuned from multiple independent places, so changing a snapping profile can leave hardcoded provider/controller behavior unchanged.
  Recommendation: Put snap provider budgets and world-span defaults into the snap profile/settings contract, then pass a normalized config to providers.

- F89 Snap diagnostics are built by two independent APIs.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-diagnostics.mjs:1-13` builds a result-level snapshot and `:16-34` builds candidate diagnostics. `bobercad/app/engine/api/interaction/snap-solver.mjs:176-203` defines a separate local `snapDiagnostic(candidate, status, reason, data = {})` with overlapping but richer fields such as `screenDistance`, `rank`, `visibilityPenaltyPx`, and `scoreBreakdown`.
  Risk: Diagnostics emitted by manager/scope/visibility paths and solver ranking paths can have different fields for the same conceptual event. QA code and debug UI must tolerate both shapes instead of one diagnostic DTO.
  Recommendation: Move snap diagnostic DTO builders to one shared module, or export the solver diagnostic builder and use it from rendering-level filters.

- F90 Snap profile defaults have two sources of truth.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-profiles.mjs:5-80` defines full runtime `DEFAULT_PROFILES` for `off`, `light`, `normal`, `strong`, and `training`. `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-settings.json:169-224` separately configures only partial `light`, `normal`, and `strong` profile values. `snapSettingsFromAuthoring` merges JSON overrides into JS defaults at `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-profiles.mjs:130-146`.
  Risk: Viewer settings are documented as the source of truth, but important profile values such as point/axis/intersection bias, `showLabels`, and the `training` profile live only in runtime code. Tuning a profile can require edits in both JSON and JS, and missing JSON fields silently inherit code defaults.
  Recommendation: Make viewer settings contain the complete snap profile contract, or move defaults to one shared JSON/config module consumed by runtime and UI metadata.

- F91 Snap scope defaults and labels have multiple partial sources.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-selection-manager.mjs:3-18` defines runtime `DEFAULT_SNAP_SCOPE`; `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-settings.json:225-240` stores the same scope flags; `bobercad/app/schemas/viewer-settings.schema.json:286-332` defines allowed scope keys; and `bobercad/app/ui/commands/snap-metadata.mjs:36-52` defines UI target/filter labels. UI metadata omits `welds` and `trimJoints`, while runtime/settings/schema still include them.
  Risk: Adding or exposing a snap scope key requires coordinated edits across runtime defaults, JSON settings, schema, and UI metadata. Hidden keys can remain configurable in settings but unreachable from controls/commands.
  Recommendation: Define one snap scope spec with defaults, schema keys, labels, and collection mapping, then generate or import it in runtime, schema validation, and UI command metadata.

- F92 Smart Component selection scope reimplements ownership traversal instead of using the project dependency API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-selection-manager.mjs:55-85` has a local `smartComponentObjectIds` that reads `project.model.smartComponentInstances`, scans `project.objectIndex`, walks `ownedObjectIds`, `objectRoles`, and `childComponentRoles`, and has its own cycle guard. The public project dependency API already exposes `smartComponentOwnedObjectIds` and `smartComponentObjectIds` at `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/dependencies.mjs:175-199`.
  Risk: Current-smart-component selection can disagree with store/API ownership, detached object ids, connection-zone object ids, filtering, and cycle behavior handled by the public dependency helper.
  Recommendation: Import or expose the project dependency/store helper to snap selection instead of maintaining a rendering-local Smart Component traversal.

- F93 Snap visibility policy hardcodes physical provider identity outside the provider registry.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-visibility-policy.mjs:37-40` treats only `model.members`, `model.plates`, and `model.fasteners` as physical snap providers. The actual provider registry is declared separately in `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:1293-1360`.
  Risk: Adding a new physical provider or changing provider ids requires a second edit in visibility policy, otherwise occlusion penalties and solid-visibility filtering silently do not apply to that provider.
  Recommendation: Put physical/visibility behavior in provider metadata or candidate visibility fields and let visibility policy read that metadata instead of duplicating provider ids.

- F94 Work-plane creation helper lives under plate-sketch API.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/work-plane-controller.mjs:3` imports `workPlaneFromThreePoints` from `engine/api/project/plate-sketch-relations-and-bends.mjs`. That barrel reexports it from `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/sketch-geometry-and-relations.mjs:143-160`, while the dedicated work-plane API module `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/work-plane.mjs` owns active plane/projection helpers but not three-point plane creation.
  Risk: A generic work-plane operation depends on the plate-sketch barrel, so future work-plane consumers can accidentally import plate-sketch geometry APIs or duplicate the helper elsewhere.
  Recommendation: Move `workPlaneFromThreePoints` into `engine/api/project/work-plane.mjs` and reexport it from the plate-sketch barrel only for backward compatibility if needed.

- F95 Scene thumbnail renderer is a parallel mini-renderer with its own projection and styling.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/preview/scene-thumbnail-renderer.mjs:85-92` projects 3D points through a local isometric formula, `:123-127` sorts faces with a local depth heuristic, and `:53-63` hardcodes fallback face/line colors, opacity, strokes, background radius, and SVG styling.
  Risk: Smart Component thumbnails can drift from actual viewer framing/color/camera behavior because they do not share viewer camera projection, scene color policy, or design tokens.
  Recommendation: Either document this module as an intentionally approximate thumbnail renderer, or feed it shared camera/color settings from the viewer render pipeline.

- F96 Member manipulator overlays duplicate coordinate-space defaults next to the shared member-axis helper.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/authoring/member-manipulator-overlays.mjs:1-5` defines its own `WORLD_AXES`, `:21-31` locally falls back axis entries to world axes plus `"local"/"global"` labels, and `:96-112` builds the global/local toggle text and labels. `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/authoring/member-axis-space.mjs:5-18` already owns world axes normalization and coordinate-space labels.
  Risk: Manipulator handles can drift from the coordinate-space labels/normalization used by member overlays, transform editing, member creation, and QA.
  Recommendation: Make `memberManipulatorHandles` consume fully normalized axis specs from `member-axis-space.mjs`, or import `normalizeCoordinateSpace`/`coordinateSpaceLabel` and remove local defaults.

- F97 Authoring overlay fallback settings are scattered and sometimes differ from viewer settings.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/authoring/member-overlays.mjs:44` and `:56` default guide spans to `1600`, while `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-settings.json:245` sets `globalAxisGuideSpan` to `12000`. The same overlay falls back to `workPlaneSize || 220` at `member-overlays.mjs:142`, `:223`, and `:227`, while settings set `workPlaneSize` to `280` at `viewer-settings.json:256`. `member-manipulator-overlays.mjs:61-72` has axis/ring defaults such as `58` and `40`, while settings define screen defaults at `viewer-settings.json:283-292`.
  Risk: Any caller that does not pass fully normalized viewer settings gets a different authoring overlay than the configured product defaults. New overlay settings can also become pseudo-settings when schema/settings are not updated.
  Recommendation: Normalize authoring overlay settings once before rendering overlays, and make overlay modules read from that normalized object without local product-value fallbacks.

- F98 Snap overlay rendering ignores the candidate preview contract and reconstructs overlays from transitional fields.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:93-94` includes a canonical `preview` field in candidate contracts, and `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-manager.mjs:71-76` exposes `preview` on accepted results. But `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/authoring/snap-overlays.mjs:21-135` derives axes/faces from flat `snap.type`, `snap.axis`, `snap.sources`, `source.kind`, `source.points`, `source.snapFacePoints`, `source.providerId`, and `source.objectId` instead of `snap.preview`.
  Risk: Provider preview metadata, solver result preview, and overlay rendering can drift. New snap candidate shapes must keep legacy `sources` conventions alive to render authoring guides.
  Recommendation: Make `snap.preview` the canonical overlay descriptor, and keep any legacy `sources` adapter in one bridge near snap result normalization.

- F99 Bend relief effective-size rules are split between renderer, controller, inspector, and normalization.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/plate-bend-geometry.mjs:10-17` computes effective relief size from `relief.type`, `relief.radius`, `relief.width`, `plate.thickness`, and `bend.radius`. `bobercad/app/engine/api/project/plate-sketch/bend-normalization.mjs:53-70` validates relief shape but does not expose effective size. `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/plate-bend-controller.mjs:72-80` chooses default bend/relief radius as `Math.max(plate.thickness || 8, 8)`, while the inspector uses a similar but separate fallback at `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-editable-object-property-metadata.mjs:289-290`.
  Risk: Rendering, creation defaults, and editable UI can disagree about the actual relief size for auto/manual/none/width/radius cases.
  Recommendation: Add one `effectiveBendRelief`/`bendReliefSize` helper next to bend normalization and use it from renderer, bend controller, and inspector metadata.

- F100 Feature reference/basis evaluation is duplicated across renderer, fastener evaluator, and snap providers.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-feature-cutters.mjs:22-58` has local `featureOrigin` for `plate-face`, `interfaceRef`, `stationReferenceInterfaceRef`, and raw reference bases. `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/evaluators/fastener-evaluator.mjs:54-98` has a second local `featureReferenceBasis` with the same domain rules. `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-candidate-providers.mjs:877-892` has a third simplified fastener snap path that reads `reference.origin`, `"plate-center"`, `feature.center`, and safe local axes directly.
  Risk: Cuts, fastener placement, and snap candidates can disagree about the same feature reference, especially around plate face offsets, `"plate-center"`, station reference interfaces, and local axis defaults.
  Recommendation: Promote one shared `featureReferenceBasis(project, profiles, feature)` evaluator and make cutters, fastener evaluation, and snap candidate providers consume it or a deliberate preview adapter around it.

- F101 Render scene output carries the mutable project model into WebGL runtime paths.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-geometry-builder.mjs:57-80` stores `project` on `sceneData` and returns it while deleting only temporary marker/settings/tessellation fields at `:140-144`. `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-highlight-policy.mjs:7-8` reads `scene.project.objectIndex` to classify highlighted objects. `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-object-preview.mjs:123-125` clones preview members from `scene.project.model.members`, `:218-219` can replace `scene.project` and then mutates `scene.project.model.members[member.id]`, and `:267` patches `scene.project` from a partial patch scene.
  Risk: Rendering/WebGL code can observe or mutate project state through the scene object instead of the store/API path, so preview patches and highlight policies become hidden model access layers.
  Recommendation: Return only render-scene metadata needed by WebGL, such as object collection lookup and preview member bases, or expose an explicit immutable scene model context instead of carrying the full project.

- F102 Render mesh edge/tolerance policy is hardcoded in scene assembly.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-line-face-assembly.mjs:128-140` quantizes mesh edge keys at `0.001` world units and sets crease detection to `15` degrees; `:162-170` uses that local policy to emit evaluated edge refs. Other rendering/annotation modules independently use `0.001` for coordinate grouping, for example `bobercad/app/rendering/annotations/dimension-geometry-and-label-context.mjs:426-446`, and trim/datum code uses tolerance-derived quantization in separate places.
  Risk: Visible crease edges, evaluated-edge snap refs, and annotation grouping can diverge when project tolerance, unit scale, or tessellation detail changes.
  Recommendation: Introduce a named render geometry tolerance/crease policy, preferably derived from project/viewer settings or the CSG tolerance layer, and use it from scene assembly and annotation grouping instead of scattering numeric thresholds.

- F103 Member feature CSG application is implemented as a renderer-private pipeline.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-member-geometry-adapters.mjs:209-260` applies hole/slot cuts, clearance cuts, boolean parts, member trim planes, member trim regions, and end-cut skips directly inside `memberCsgPolygons`; unsupported feature types throw from this renderer module at `:259`. The engine geometry layer exposes member frames/interfaces in `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/member-evaluator.mjs`, but there is no shared `member feature -> polygons` evaluator for render/export/analysis callers.
  Risk: Any future exporter, analyzer, thumbnail, or non-scene geometry path must either call rendering code or reimplement the feature dispatch, making member geometry semantics renderer-owned.
  Recommendation: Move feature application into an engine geometry evaluator such as `evaluateMemberPolygons`/`applyMemberFeatures`, with scene adapters only converting evaluated polygons to faces/edges.

- F104 Boolean feature operation values are repeated across schema, UI, and scene adapters.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/schemas/project.schema.json:1822-1827` defines enum values `BOOLEAN_CUT`, `BOOLEAN_ADD`, and `BOOLEAN_WELDPREP`; `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-editable-object-property-metadata.mjs:4-7`, `:91-98`, and `:345-347` duplicate UI options/defaults; `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-object-geometry-adapters.mjs:142-147` and `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-member-geometry-adapters.mjs:233-237` independently validate and interpret the same values.
  Risk: Adding or renaming a boolean operation requires synchronized edits across schema, inspector UI, object rendering, and member rendering. Defaults can also drift because the UI assumes `BOOLEAN_CUT` when absent while renderers validate actual values differently.
  Recommendation: Export one boolean feature operation registry/metadata object used by schema generation or schema-adjacent validation, inspector options, and render/evaluator operation dispatch.

- F105 Plate solid feature application is renderer-private and bent plates have a separate unsupported path.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-object-geometry-adapters.mjs:72-89` renders bent plates through `plateBendGeometry`, while `:91-122` applies flat-plate CSG features locally in `plateCsgPolygons`. `addPlate` rejects bent plates with any `featureIds` at `:125-129` with "bent plate features are not implemented in strict evaluator".
  Risk: Flat plates and bent plates follow different geometry contracts, and non-render consumers cannot reuse an engine-level evaluated plate solid. Feature support can diverge between viewer, export, and future analysis paths.
  Recommendation: Move plate solid evaluation, including flat/bent feature handling, into an engine geometry evaluator; keep the scene adapter responsible only for converting evaluated panels/polygons to faces and edges.

- F106 Fastener visual assembly dimensions are derived only in the scene adapter.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/engine/geometry/evaluators/fastener-evaluator.mjs:153-179` evaluates basis, axis, grip length, and positions, but not head/nut/washer visual dimensions. `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/scene-object-geometry-adapters.mjs:154-201` derives shank radius, head height/across-flats, nut dimensions, washer radii, default bolt length, washer placement, and picking radius from renderer-local fallbacks such as `shankDiameter * 0.6`, `shankDiameter * 1.5`, `headAcrossFlats * 1.25`, `shankDiameter + 2`, render fastener length, and minimum pick radius `60`.
  Risk: Rendering can show bolt/nut/washer proportions that are not part of the fastener evaluator/catalog contract, so export, selection envelopes, thumbnails, and future fabrication checks may disagree about the same fastener assembly.
  Recommendation: Extend the fastener evaluator with an evaluated assembly/visual envelope DTO, or create a shared fastener geometry policy consumed by renderer and any export/analysis path.

- F107 Camera direction-to-angle conversion is duplicated in QA view code.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-view-state.mjs:7-12` exports `cameraAnglesForDirection`. `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-qa-bridge.mjs:125-130` reimplements the same yaw/pitch math locally instead of importing the WebGL view-state helper, and QA view helpers build additional hardcoded view directions at `:110-143`.
  Risk: QA screenshots/smoke views can drift from runtime viewer orientation math, so automated visual checks may pass/fail against a camera state that normal UI paths cannot reproduce.
  Recommendation: Import `cameraAnglesForDirection`/orientation helpers from `webgl-view-state.mjs` into QA bridge, and keep any QA-specific view names as data that uses the shared conversion.

- F108 Dimension label presentation is resolved separately in WebGL and DOM overlay paths.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/text-label-renderer.mjs:7-29` defines `labelText`, `textSettings`, hover color `#2563eb`, default label color `#334155`, font family/weight/min-size fallbacks, and draw eligibility. `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/dimensions/dimension-overlay-ui.mjs:5`, `:421-431`, and `:497-502` repeat hover color, label text height, font family/weight/min-size, and hover color application for active/editing DOM labels.
  Risk: Inactive WebGL labels and active/editable DOM labels can render with different fallback font/color/min-size behavior even though they represent the same dimension labels.
  Recommendation: Extract a shared dimension label presentation resolver that returns text, font family/weight/size thresholds, hover color, and fallback color for both renderers.

- F109 WebGL object preview mutates the live render scene as a parallel scene patch store.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-object-preview.mjs:172-199` mutates point arrays and LOD detail centers in-place for translated scene objects. `:201-228` updates member instance transforms, can replace `scene.project`, and writes `scene.project.model.members[member.id] = member`. `:231-275` replaces live `scene.faces`, `scene.lines`, `scene.callouts`, `scene.memberInstances`, LOD maps, empty LOD sets, scene activity ids, and generated-object sets from a patch scene.
  Risk: The preview controller can diverge from `buildScene`/render scheduler semantics and must manually remember every scene-owned cache/collection to invalidate or patch. It also gives preview code a hidden model mutation channel through `scene.project`.
  Recommendation: Define an explicit scene patch API/DTO owned by the render scheduler or scene builder, and keep preview controllers from mutating arbitrary scene collections/project state directly.

- F110 WebGL picker hit tolerances are hardcoded separately from snap/viewer policy.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-picker.mjs:3-18` uses barycentric tolerances `0.000001` and `-0.0001`; `:111-117` uses line-length tolerance `1e-9`; `:119-153` clamps instanced-member hit threshold to `6..16` pixels; `:294-329` clamps snap visibility sample radius to `0..4` pixels and samples only center plus four cardinal offsets. Snap visibility policy/settings are handled separately in `bobercad/app/rendering/interaction/snap-visibility-policy.mjs`.
  Risk: Picking, orbit anchors, and snap visibility can disagree about what is close enough, especially between CPU/GPU pick paths and snap profile settings.
  Recommendation: Move picker tolerances into a named WebGL picking policy or pass them from the existing snap/viewer settings context so picker, snap visibility, and interaction profiles share one contract.

- F111 Instanced-member shader normal transform is malformed.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-programs.mjs:139-145` computes world position with `aAxisX`, `aAxisY`, and `aAxisZ`, but computes normal as `normalize(aAxisX * aLocalNormal.x + aLocalNormal.y + aAxisZ * aLocalNormal.z)`, missing `aAxisY * aLocalNormal.y`.
  Risk: Instanced member lighting is wrong and the shader may fail to compile on GLSL implementations that reject vector-plus-scalar arithmetic.
  Recommendation: Change the normal transform to `normalize(aAxisX * aLocalNormal.x + aAxisY * aLocalNormal.y + aAxisZ * aLocalNormal.z)` and add a render smoke check for instanced member shading.

- F112 WebGL shader/program creation is duplicated outside the program registry.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-programs.mjs:41-55` defines `compileShader` and `createProgram` inside the program registry. `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/text-label-renderer.mjs:49-77` reimplements shader compilation/linking locally for label rendering.
  Risk: Shader error handling, lifecycle, and future WebGL compatibility fixes must be applied in multiple places.
  Recommendation: Export a small shared WebGL program helper or let `webgl-programs.mjs` own text label program creation too.

- F113 Dimension hide-behind-geometry setting is ignored by the WebGL orchestrator.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-render-orchestrator.mjs:98-100` defines `hideDimensionsBehindGeometry()` as unconditional `return false`; `:846-850` and `:854-862` pass that value into dimension line/label drawing. `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-settings.json:338` and `bobercad/app/schemas/viewer-settings.schema.json:678-679` expose `render.dimensions.hideBehindGeometry` as a settings contract.
  Risk: The schema/settings surface promises a dimension occlusion option that runtime rendering can never enable.
  Recommendation: Resolve this through a named render-dimension policy, or at minimum return `settings.render.dimensions?.hideBehindGeometry === true` from the orchestrator helper.

- F114 `appendWorldVertex` carries a dual calling convention compatibility overload.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-render-orchestrator.mjs:225-239` accepts either a render group object or raw `positions/colors` arrays by detecting `Array.isArray(group) && Array.isArray(point) && Array.isArray(rgba)`, then reassigns parameters before writing the vertex. Non-array color input silently returns.
  Risk: Static render cache construction can accept mismatched argument shapes without a clear failure, and future buffer writers must preserve both calling conventions.
  Recommendation: Split this into explicit helpers, for example `appendGroupVertex(group, point, rgba, pickRgba)` and `appendArrayVertex(positions, colors, point, rgba)`, so render-group and raw-array writes have one contract each.

- F115 WebGL pointer controls hardcode trim-region click priority.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-viewer-controls.mjs:305-310` handles a pending-orbit pointerup by forcing `pickScene(..., { forceCpu: true, includeInstances: false, componentKind: "trim-region" })` before falling back to the current drag face or generic click pick.
  Risk: Component-specific click behavior is embedded in low-level WebGL pointer controls, so other click entry points can drift and future component pick priorities require editing this controls layer.
  Recommendation: Move click-priority policy into the picker/runtime interaction contract, for example as a supplied click-pick profile or click handler option, and keep `webgl-viewer-controls.mjs` responsible only for event sequencing.

- F116 WebGL large-scene threshold is duplicated as an unnamed constant.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-highlight-policy.mjs:3-5` treats scenes with more than `25000` render items as large for highlight optimization. `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-viewer-runtime.mjs:242-244` independently switches to GPU picking when faces plus member instances exceed `25000`.
  Risk: Highlight optimization and pick strategy can diverge when performance thresholds change, and the value is not visible through viewer settings or a named WebGL policy.
  Recommendation: Move the threshold into one WebGL scene-performance policy, preferably with separate named fields if highlight and picking should eventually differ.

- F117 Authoring handle contracts are implicit across overlay generation, hit testing, and rendering.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-viewer-runtime.mjs:525-619` constructs hover keys and hit-tests handles by `type`, `kind`, `axisId`, `dragAxes`, `hitTolerancePx`, `radius`, and `pickPriority`; `bobercad/app/rendering/webgl/webgl-render-orchestrator.mjs:109-176` and `:777-815` render axis/ring/point handles from overlapping fields. Overlay generators such as `bobercad/app/rendering/scene/authoring/member-manipulator-overlays.mjs:115-155` create those descriptors.
  Risk: A new handle shape must be manually understood by at least the overlay generator, WebGL hit-test path, and WebGL render path, with no schema or adapter enforcing the shared contract.
  Recommendation: Add a small authoring-handle descriptor API that normalizes type/kind/default/tolerance fields, then make generators, hit testing, and rendering consume that normalized contract.

- F118 Ribbon section grouping is inferred from command-id substrings.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/command-group-metadata.mjs:80-104` routes commands to ribbon sections by checking whether `command.id` includes substrings such as `.beam.`, `.column.`, `.plate`, `.bend`, `.connection`, `.weld`, `.bolt`, `.sketch`, `.workPlane`, `dimension`, `clash`, `.displayMode.`, and `.orientation.`.
  Risk: Renaming command ids or adding a command with an overlapping substring can silently move it to a different UI section; command grouping is not validated as command metadata.
  Recommendation: Add explicit `ribbonSection` or `section` metadata to command specs, keep this inference only as a migration/default bridge, and validate section ids against `RIBBON_SECTION_ORDER`.

- F119 Generated command action names depend on UI labels.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/command-registry.mjs:247-265` builds `VIEW_ORIENTATION_COMMANDS` and `DISPLAY_MODE_COMMANDS` actions from `spec.label`; `:320-322` builds selection-scope actions from `mode.label`; `:383-398` builds snap-strength/snap-target actions from labels/keys.
  Risk: Changing visible labels or punctuation can change the handler action string, so display copy edits can break command execution wiring.
  Recommendation: Generate action names from stable ids or define explicit `action` fields in the source metadata specs, then treat labels as presentation-only.

- F120 Data library descriptor default status is effectively unreachable with omitted config.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/data-surface-metadata.mjs:67` defaults `config = {}`; `:77` computes `status` as `count !== null ? "loaded" : (config ? "declared" : "default")`. The default `{}` is truthy, so calling `dataLibraryDescriptor(libraryId)` reports `"declared"` rather than `"default"`.
  Risk: UI/search metadata can report an undeclared library as declared, hiding the distinction between default/fallback library specs and configured library packs.
  Recommendation: Default `config` to `null`, or compute declaration from actual config keys such as `libraryId`, `version`, or `path`.

- F121 Inspector section placement is inferred from ids, labels, and field shapes.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-property-metadata.mjs:75-83` returns `"diagnostics"` if the section id includes `diagnostic` or fields include error/warning states, returns `"actions"` if every field is an action, returns `"reference"` if id or label includes `reference`, otherwise returns `"main"`.

  Recommendation: Require explicit `placement` in section factories, or use named section-builder helpers that set placement while keeping this heuristic only as a temporary compatibility bridge.

- F122 Active-tool guidance is keyed separately from command metadata.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-property-metadata.mjs:15-49` defines `ACTIVE_TOOL_HINTS` keyed by command ids such as `model.beam.create`, `model.column.create`, and `model.trim.create`, while the command records themselves live in `bobercad/app/ui/commands/command-registry.mjs:17-122`.
  Risk: Adding, renaming, or deleting commands requires synchronized edits in command registry and inspector metadata, and missing hints are silent.

- F123 Grid inspector falls back from missing grid level ids to every project level.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/inspector-support-object-property-metadata.mjs:219-226` sets `levelIds` to `gridSystem.levelIds` when present, otherwise to `Object.keys(projectLevels)`, then builds editable level fields from those levels.

- F124 Model search descriptors keep multiple semantic alias fields alive.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/commands/model-collection-metadata.mjs:129-138` builds search keywords by trying alternate paths such as `profileRef`, `profile`, `sectionProfileRef`, `materialRef`, `material`, `fastenerRef`, `catalogRef`, `catalogEntryRef`, `componentRef`, `definitionRef`, `smartComponentRef`, and `smartComponentId`.

- F125 Display mode normalization is duplicated between UI metadata and WebGL view state.

- F126 Design-system disclosure sections own workspace persistence.

- F127 Command enabled/disabled semantics are duplicated across UI command surfaces.

- F128 Command palette recents use a separate browser storage path outside workspace preferences.

- F129 Dock tab reveal logic bypasses the panel reveal synchronization API.

- F130 Inspector dock reimplements dock-tab behavior instead of sharing the dock-tab controller.

- F131 Viewer overlay corner specs are duplicated across workspace modules.

- F132 Workspace customizer label fallback uses a local `titleCase` instead of the shared labels helper.

- F133 Toolbar dock default is duplicated instead of sourced from the workspace state normalizer.

  Risk: If toolbar docking is reintroduced or the default changes, state normalization, manager DOM state, and dialog defaults can diverge.

- F134 Workspace toolbar drag target is hardcoded to `#modeling-toolbar`.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/shell/workspace-customizer-manager.mjs:16` accepts a `toolbar` element, but `toolbarButtonAt()` at `:1114-1116` finds drop targets with `document.elementFromPoint(...).closest("#modeling-toolbar .bc-toolbar-command-draggable")`.

- F135 Workspace ordering repeats the same list-move algorithms per collection.

- F136 Workspace/id validators are duplicated across shell modules.

- F137 CSS selector escaping fallback is duplicated and inconsistent.

- F138 Workspace import uses a partial manual shape check instead of the UI workspace schema contract.

- F139 Dimension overlay rendering bypasses the Smart Component API accessor.

- F140 Dimension overlay reimplements tooltip/control primitives outside the shared UI helpers.

- F141 Plate sketch inspector duplicates public sketch geometry helper APIs.

- F143 Smart Component quick-parameter wrapper keeps a local catalog-options compatibility adapter.
