- F144 Feature editing has two parallel descriptor/commit stacks for the same store APIs.
  Evidence: The dedicated feature editor defines `feature.operationEnabled.set`, `feature.update`, `feature.body.update`, `feature.body.outlinePoint.update`, and `feature.source.update` bindings in `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/feature-editor-panel.mjs:34-60`.   Risk: Feature body center/size/radius/depth/boolean enabled behavior can diverge between the object inspector and the feature editor. Any validation, min/max options, vector handling, affected-object calculation, or source-member restriction must be updated in two places.
  Recommendation: Define one feature-edit descriptor/action contract and let the compact object inspector and expanded feature editor select different subsets/views of that same contract, or route both namespaces through one adapter with shared patch construction.

- F145 Generated property binding silently no-ops on unknown commit/action/command ids.
  Evidence: `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/panels/generated-property-bindings.mjs:28-38` installs `onChange`, `onClick`, and `onCustom` handlers when descriptors contain `commit`, `commandId`, `action`, or `customAction`; the actual dispatchers at `:128-138` use optional chaining (`bindings.commits?.[action]?.(...)`, `bindings.runCommand?.(...)`, `bindings.actions?.[action]?.(...)`) and return `undefined` when the binding is missing. By contrast, `bobercad/app/ui/viewer/viewer-app-controller.mjs:42-45` throws when a registered viewer command id is missing.
  Risk: A typo or stale action id in generated property metadata can render an apparently editable field/button that does nothing, hiding broken API wiring until manual UI testing.
  Recommendation: Add a descriptor-binding validation mode or fail/log loudly for unknown commit/action/command ids at bind time. Intentional optional actions should be marked explicitly as optional/disabled instead of falling through optional chaining.

- F146 Custom-profile authoring defaults are owned by the inspector UI instead of the profile API/defaults.

Detailed manual function/API audit protocol - added after user correction on 2026-06-29:
- The earlier manual pass is not detailed enough for the requested standard.
- New required sequence for each source file:
  1. List all exports, function declarations, local helper functions, arrow/function-expression helpers, and object-returned API methods.
  2. State what the file/folder appears responsible for.
  3. Check whether every listed function belongs in that file/folder or looks misplaced.
  4. Compare function names and responsibilities against the global function inventory to find repeated implementations.
  5. Check whether public behavior goes through the intended API layer or bypasses it with direct model/ctx/store access.
  6. Record fallbacks, compatibility branches, alternate data shapes, hidden defaults, and placeholder/no-op behavior with line references.
  7. Record a per-file verdict: OK, follow-up, or finding.
- A generated function inventory may be used only as a navigation/index aid. Findings must still be confirmed by reading the relevant source manually.
- Generated navigation index: `function-api-inventory.txt`.
  - Indexed 233 app JS/MJS files.
  - Indexed 4701 function/method-like entries.
  - Found 435 repeated function/method names.
- All-files target:
  - `bobercad/app` contains 283 files.
  - 276 are text/reviewable files: `.mjs`, `.js`, `.json`, `.css`, `.html`, `.md`.
  - 7 are binary/asset files and must still be inventoried for role, location, naming, and references, but they have no functions/lines to audit in the function matrix.
  - JS/MJS files use the full function/API matrix. Non-JS text files use a reduced matrix: file role, schema/config/CSS selectors or docs sections, duplication/compat markers, API/data contract references, and verdict.
- Detailed function/API pass progress: all 276 text/reviewable app files reviewed with the new matrix, 72178 physical source lines. All 7 app binary/assets are now inventoried below.

Repository remainder method:
- Data `.mjs` files use the same function/API matrix as app/support code: function list, file/folder fit, duplicate logic, Smart Component API routing, fallback/default/compatibility checks, and verdict.
- Data JSON/MD files use a reduced contract/data matrix: schema/register/library role, stale fields such as removed `connections`, old `componentRef` terminology, fallback defaults, generated-data provenance, cross-file references, and verdict. Very large generated sample JSON is parsed and structurally checked, then sampled around flagged/stale fields rather than pasted into the report line-by-line.
- Root/tmp/audit artifacts are accounted for as repo files; generated audit artifacts and temporary logs/images are inventoried so they are not mistaken for unreviewed app behavior.

- `bobercad/app/engine/api/api-register.json` - 1592 lines, 161 API entries.
  File/folder role:
  - JSON API manifest for engine/store/Smart Component runtime APIs. It belongs under `engine/api` as a catalog/contract file, not implementation.
  Functions in file:
  - None; JSON manifest only.
  API surface listed:
  - Includes store API, project API, Smart Component `ctx.*`, model geometry/check/semantic builder APIs, compliance, sectioning, and connection primitive entries.
  Fit to folder:
  - Fits as a high-level API register, but it mixes documentation quality: some entries have domain descriptions, many store entries use generated text such as "Public project store API for ..." and parameters named "method parameter".
  Duplicate/overlap checks:
  - `ctx.param`, `ctx.parameterValue`, `ctx.requiredInput`, and `ctx.params` all expose parameter/input reads from Smart Component runtime. This can be valid, but it needs clear policy because generators currently mix raw `ctx.param` and default-aware `ctx.parameterValue` (F17).
  - Member edit APIs appear as a cluster: `store.moveMember`, `store.moveMemberWithLayout`, `store.setMemberCenter`, `store.setMemberEndpoints`, `store.setMemberLayoutEndpoint`, `store.setMemberPhysicalEndpoint`, and `store.updateMember`; implementation review must verify one shared endpoint/layout-axis behavior.
  - Smart Component ownership APIs appear as a cluster: `store.smartComponentForObject`, `store.smartComponentObjectIds`, `store.smartComponentRoot`, `store.smartComponentRootForObject`; implementation review must verify one shared ownership traversal.
  API path / bypass check:
  - Register says `geometry.paths` maps to `./geometry/paths.mjs`, but does not enumerate the concrete exports inside that module. Direct imports also exist from rendering and transport code, so this module is not only accessed through the register.
  Verdict:
  - Follow-up. The manifest belongs here, but API documentation and grouped overlapping APIs need deeper implementation review before they can be called standardized.
